title.zh: 卷一百五十七 列傳第八十二 陸贄
title.raw: 卷一百五十七 列傳第八十二 陸贄 Volume 157 Biographies 82: Lu Zhi

sentences.zh: 陸贄，字敬輿，蘇州嘉興人。

translations.literal: Lu Zai, style name Jingyu, was a man of Jiaxing in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zai, whose courtesy name was Jingyu, came from Jiaxing in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 十八第進士，中博學宏辭。

translations.literal: At eighteen he ranked first in the jinshi examination and passed the erudite and comprehensive discourse examination.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he took first place in the jinshi examination and also passed the boxue hongci examination.

sentences.zh: 調鄭尉，罷歸。

translations.literal: He was assigned as Wei of Zheng, then dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Zheng county, then dismissed and went home.

sentences.zh: 壽州刺史張鎰有重名，贄往見，語三日，奇之，請為忘年交。

translations.literal: Zhang Yin, prefect of Shouzhou, had a great reputation. Zai went to see him; they spoke for three days. Zhang marveled at him and asked to become friends despite their age difference.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yin, prefect of Shouzhou, was widely esteemed. Zai called on him, and after three days of conversation Zhang was so impressed that he proposed a friendship that ignored their difference in years.

sentences.zh: 既行，餉錢百萬，曰：「請為母夫人一日費。」

translations.literal: When Zai was about to leave, [Zhang] presented a million in cash, saying: "Please accept this as one day's expenses for your mother.
translations.idiomatic: As Zai was leaving, Zhang offered him a million cash and said, "Please take this for your mother's daily needs.

sentences.zh: 贄不納，止受茶一串，曰：「敢不承公之賜？」

translations.literal: Zai would not accept it, taking only a string of tea, and said: "How dare I not accept your gift?"
translations.idiomatic: Zai refused the money, accepting only a string of tea, and said, "How could I not acknowledge your kindness?"

sentences.zh: 以書判拔萃補渭南尉。

translations.literal: Through excellence in the book-judgment examination he was appointed supplemental Wei of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed recorder at Weinan after distinguishing himself in the book-judgment examination.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，遣黜陟使庾何等十一人行天下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, he dispatched eleven promotion-and-demotion commissioners including Yu He to travel throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong came to the throne, he sent eleven promotion-and-demotion commissioners, including Yu He, to tour the empire.

sentences.zh: 贄說使者，請以五術省風俗，八計聽吏治，三科登雋乂，四賦經財實，六德保罷瘵，五要簡官事。

translations.literal: Zai persuaded the commissioners, asking that they use five methods to examine local customs, eight reckonings to hear official governance, three categories to elevate outstanding talent, four levies to manage fiscal realities, six virtues to protect the exhausted and afflicted, and five essentials to streamline government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zai urged the commissioners to inspect customs through five methods, assess official governance through eight reckonings, promote talent through three categories, regulate finances through four levies, relieve the worn and sick through six virtues, and streamline administration through five essentials.

sentences.zh: 五術曰：「聽謠誦審其哀樂，納市賈觀其好惡，訊簿書考其爭訟，覽車服等其儉奢，省作業察其趣舍。」

translations.literal: The five methods were: "Listen to ballads and songs to discern joy and sorrow; receive merchants and observe likes and dislikes; question ledgers and examine litigation; review carriages and dress to compare thrift and extravagance; inspect occupations and observe pursuits and withdrawals.
translations.idiomatic: The five methods were: listen to folk songs to gauge public mood; consult merchants to learn what people favor or reject; examine registers to study lawsuits; review carriages and dress to compare thrift with extravagance; and inspect trades to see what people pursue or abandon.

sentences.zh: 八計曰：「視戶口豐耗以稽撫字，視墾田贏縮以稽本末，視賦役薄厚以稽廉冒，視案籍煩簡以稽聽斷，視囚系盈虛以稽決滯，視奸盜有無以稽禁禦，視選舉眾寡以稽風化，視學校興廢以稽教導。」

translations.literal: The eight reckonings were: "Observe whether households are abundant or depleted to audit nurturing governance; observe whether reclaimed fields expand or shrink to audit root and branch; observe whether taxes and corvée are light or heavy to audit integrity and graft; observe whether case records are cumbersome or simple to audit hearings and judgments; observe whether prisoners are many or few to audit delays in decisions; observe whether banditry exists to audit prohibition and defense; observe whether selections are numerous or sparse to audit moral transformation; observe whether schools flourish or decline to audit instruction and guidance."
translations.idiomatic: The eight reckonings were: household growth or decline to judge how well officials nurture the people; reclaimed land gained or lost to judge agricultural fundamentals; tax and corvée burdens to judge honesty and corruption; case records to judge how cases are heard; prison populations to judge backlog in justice; crime to judge policing; recruitment numbers to judge moral influence; and schools to judge education.

sentences.zh: 三科曰：「茂異，賢良，幹蠱。」

translations.literal: The three categories were: "Outstanding excellence, worthy integrity, and ability to resolve difficulties."
translations.idiomatic: The three categories were outstanding excellence, worthy integrity, and proven ability to resolve crises.

sentences.zh: 四賦曰：「閱稼以奠稅，度產以衰征，料丁壯以計庸，占商賈以均利。」

translations.literal: The four levies were: "Inspect crops to fix grain tax, measure output to adjust proportional levies, count able-bodied men to calculate corvée labor, and assess merchants to equalize profits."
translations.idiomatic: The four levies were: inspect harvests to set grain tax; measure output to adjust proportional levies; count able-bodied men for corvée; and assess merchants to balance commercial profits.

sentences.zh: 六德曰：「敬老，慈幼，救疾，恤孤，賑貧窮，任失業。」

translations.literal: The six virtues were: "Honor the aged, cherish the young, rescue the sick, pity orphans, relieve the poor, and employ the unemployed."
translations.idiomatic: The six virtues were honoring the aged, cherishing the young, treating the sick, caring for orphans, relieving poverty, and finding work for the unemployed.

sentences.zh: 五要曰：「廢兵之冗食，蠲法之撓人，省官之不急，去物之無用，罷事之非要。」

translations.literal: The five essentials were: "Abolish redundant military rations, repeal laws that harass the people, reduce nonessential offices, remove useless goods, and end nonessential undertakings."
translations.idiomatic: The five essentials were eliminating redundant military provisions, repealing oppressive laws, cutting nonessential offices, removing useless expenditures, and ending unnecessary projects.

sentences.zh: 時皆韙其言。

translations.literal: At the time all approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone at the time endorsed his proposals.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮，已聞其名矣，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: While the emperor was still heir apparent, he had already heard Zai's name and summoned him as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already heard of him when he was still crown prince, and on accession he summoned Zai to serve as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 會馬燧討賊河北，久不決，請濟師；

translations.literal: It happened that Ma Sui was campaigning against rebels in Hebei without a swift decision and requested reinforcements;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ma Sui was campaigning against rebels in Hebei without achieving a quick victory and asked for reinforcements;

sentences.zh: 李希烈寇襄城。

translations.literal: Li Xilie raided Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: while Li Xilie was attacking Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 詔問策安出，贄言：

translations.literal: An edict asked where strategy should come from. Zai said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what policy should be adopted. Zai replied:

sentences.zh: 勞於服遠，莫若脩近；

translations.literal: To weary oneself serving the distant, nothing is better than repairing what is near;
translations.idiomatic: When effort is wasted on distant campaigns, nothing works better than securing what is close at hand;

sentences.zh: 多方以救失，莫若改行。

translations.literal: to use many expedients to remedy failure, nothing is better than changing course.
translations.idiomatic: and when many expedients are tried to repair a mistake, nothing works better than changing course.

sentences.zh: 今幽、燕、恒、魏之勢緩而禍輕，汝、洛、滎、汴之勢急而禍重。

translations.literal: Now the situation in You, Yan, Heng, and Wei is slack and the peril light, while that in Ru, Luo, Ying, and Bian is urgent and the peril grave.
translations.idiomatic: At present the threat from You, Yan, Heng, and Wei is slack and the danger comparatively light, whereas that from Ru, Luo, Ying, and Bian is urgent and the danger grave.

sentences.zh: 田悅覆敗之餘，無復遠略，王武俊有勇無謀，朱滔多疑少決，互相制劫，急則合力，退則背憎，不能有越軼之患，此謂緩也。

translations.literal: Tian Yue, after his overthrow and defeat, has no further long-range designs; Wang Wujun has courage but no strategy; Zhu Tao is suspicious and slow to decide. They restrain and coerce one another—when pressed they unite, when they withdraw they turn on each other in hatred—and cannot produce a threat of overstepping bounds. This is what is called slack.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue, shattered in defeat, no longer has grand ambitions; Wang Wujun is brave but lacks strategy; Zhu Tao is suspicious and indecisive. They check and coerce one another—uniting only under pressure, turning on one another when they pull back—and cannot mount a threat that truly overruns the court. That is the slack danger.

sentences.zh: 希烈果於奔噬，忍於傷殘，據蔡、許富全之地，而益以鄧、襄虜獲之實，東寇則餉道阻，北窺則都邑震，此謂急也。

translations.literal: Xilie is bold in rushing to devour, ruthless in injury and slaughter. He holds the rich and complete territory of Cai and Xu and adds the booty of Deng and Xiang. If he raids eastward, supply lines are blocked; if he looks northward, the capital trembles. This is what is called urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie is swift to strike and ruthless in destruction. He holds the wealthy regions of Cai and Xu and has added the spoils of Deng and Xiang. An eastern raid would cut supply routes; a northern thrust would shake the capital. That is the urgent danger.

sentences.zh: 代、朔、邠、靈自昔之精騎，上黨、盟津今之選師，舉而委之山東，將多而勢分，兵廣而財屈，則屯戍失於太繁也。

translations.literal: The elite cavalry of Dai, Shuofang, Bin, and Lingzhou from old, and the picked armies of Shangdang and Mengjin today, have all been committed to Shandong. Generals are many and power divided; troops are broad and finances strained—thus garrison deployment errs on the side of excess.
translations.idiomatic: The famed cavalry of Dai, Shuofang, Bin, and Ling, together with the picked forces of Shangdang and Mengjin, have all been thrown into Shandong. Too many generals divide command; too many troops exhaust funds—garrisons have been spread too thin.

sentences.zh: 李勉，文吏也，而當汴必爭地；

translations.literal: Li Mian is a civil official, yet he faces Bian, ground that must be contested;
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian is a civil official, yet he must hold contested ground at Bian;

sentences.zh: 哥舒曜之眾，烏合也，扞襄城方銳之賊。

translations.literal: the troops of Ge Shuyao are a mob, yet they must resist at Xiangcheng a foe at the height of its sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shuyao's men are a hastily gathered force, yet they must hold Xiangcheng against an enemy at the peak of its power.

sentences.zh: 本非素習，首鼠莫前，則守禦失於不足也。

translations.literal: They are not trained by long habit and hang back undecided—thus defense errs on the side of insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Untrained and hesitant, they cannot advance—defense has been left too weak.

sentences.zh: 今若還李芃河陽以援東都，李懷光解襄城之圍，專以太原、澤、潞兵抗山東，則梁、宋安。

translations.literal: If now Li Pi is returned to Heyang to aid the eastern capital, Li Huaiguang lifts the siege of Xiangcheng, and the armies of Taiyuan, Ze, and Lu are devoted solely to resisting Shandong, then Liang and Song will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: If Li Pi is sent back to Heyang to relieve the eastern capital, Li Huaiguang lifts the siege of Xiangcheng, and the Taiyuan, Ze, and Lu armies are concentrated against Shandong alone, then Liang and Song will be secure.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He went on to say:

sentences.zh: 立國之權，在審輕重，本大而末小，所以能固。

translations.literal: The power of establishing a state lies in discerning what is heavy and what is light; when the root is large and the branches small, it can be secure.
translations.idiomatic: The power to found and hold a state lies in judging what is heavy and what is light; when the root is strong and the branches small, the realm can stand firm.

sentences.zh: 故治天下者，若身使臂，臂使指，小大適稱而不悖。

translations.literal: Thus one who governs all under Heaven is like the body commanding the arm and the arm commanding the fingers—great and small properly matched without contradiction.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler should govern the realm as the body commands the arm and the arm the fingers, with each part properly proportioned and none working at cross purposes.

sentences.zh: 王畿者，四方之本也；

translations.literal: The royal domain is the root of the four quarters;
translations.idiomatic: The royal domain is the foundation of the four quarters;

sentences.zh: 京邑者，王畿之本也。

translations.literal: the capital region is the root of the royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: and the capital is the foundation of the royal domain.

sentences.zh: 其勢當京邑如身，王畿如臂，而四方如指，此天子大權也。

translations.literal: In disposition the capital should be like the body, the royal domain like the arm, and the four quarters like the fingers—this is the great power of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The capital should stand like the body, the royal domain like the arm, and the provinces like the fingers—that is the great leverage of the throne.

sentences.zh: 是以前世轉天下租稅，徙郡縣豪傑，以實京師。

translations.literal: Therefore in former ages they shifted the empire's tax grain and moved county and district magnates to fill the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That is why earlier dynasties diverted the empire's tax revenues and moved local elites to strengthen the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗列置府兵八百所，而關中五百，舉天下不敵關中，則居重馭輕之意也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong arrayed eight hundred garrison-militia posts, five hundred of them in Guanzhong, so that all under Heaven could not match Guanzhong—this was the idea of occupying the heavy to control the light.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong established eight hundred militia posts, five hundred in Guanzhong alone, so that the whole empire could not outweigh the center—that was the principle of holding the heavy to command the light.

sentences.zh: 方世承平久，武備微，故祿山乘外重之勢，一舉而覆兩京。

translations.literal: When the age had long enjoyed peace, military preparations were slight, so Lushan exploited the weight of the outer regions and in one stroke overturned the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: After long peace military readiness had weakened, and An Lushan exploited the strength of the frontier armies to overturn both capitals in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 然猶諸牧有馬，州縣有糧，肅宗得以中興。

translations.literal: Yet the various prefectures still had horses and the counties and districts still had grain, so Emperor Suzong was able to restore the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the provinces still had horses and the districts grain, so Suzong was able to restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 乾元後，外虞踵發，悉師東討，故吐蕃乘虛，而先帝莫與為禦，是失馭輕之權也。

translations.literal: After the Qianyuan era foreign alarms came in succession and all armies were sent east to campaign, so Tibet seized the opening and the late emperor had none to resist with—this was the loss of the power to control the light.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianyuan, foreign threats followed one after another and every army was sent east, so Tibet seized the opening and the late emperor had no force left to resist—control of the lighter parts of the realm had been lost.

sentences.zh: 既自陜還，懲乂前事，稍益禁衛，故關中有朔方、涇原、隴右之兵以捍西戎，河東有太原之兵以制北虜。

translations.literal: After returning from Shaan, he corrected the errors of the past and gradually increased the palace guard, so that in Guanzhong there were the armies of Shuofang, Jingyuan, and Longyou to repel the western barbarians, and in Hedong the army of Taiyuan to restrain the northern foes.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from Shaan he learned from past mistakes and strengthened the palace guard, posting Shuofang, Jingyuan, and Longyou troops in Guanzhong against the western frontier and the Taiyuan army in Hedong against the north.

sentences.zh: 今朔方、太原眾已屯山東，而神策六軍悉戍關外，將不能盡敵，則請濟師。

translations.literal: Now the masses of Shuofang and Taiyuan are already encamped in Shandong, while the six Shence armies are all garrisoned outside the passes. The generals cannot overcome the enemy fully, and so they request reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Shuofang and Taiyuan forces are already in Shandong, while all six Shence armies are posted outside the passes. Unable to defeat the enemy, the commanders ask for more troops.

sentences.zh: 陛下為之輟邊軍，缺環衛，竭內廄之馬、武庫之兵，占將家子以益師，賦私畜以增騎。

translations.literal: Your Majesty for this purpose has withdrawn frontier armies, left the palace guard short, exhausted the horses of the inner stud and the weapons of the arsenal, impressed the sons of general families to enlarge the army, and levied private livestock to increase cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has stripped the frontier, weakened the palace guard, emptied the imperial stables and arsenals, impressed the sons of military families into service, and levied private livestock to mount more cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又告乏財，則為算室廬，貸商人，設諸榷之科，日日以甚。

translations.literal: When funds were again reported insufficient, there were assessments on dwellings, loans to merchants, and the establishment of every sort of monopoly levy, growing worse day by day.
translations.idiomatic: When funds ran short again, houses were assessed, merchants were forced to lend, and every kind of monopoly tax was imposed—each day the burden grew heavier.

sentences.zh: 萬有一如朱滔、李希烈負固邊壘，竊發都甸者，何以備之？

translations.literal: If by any chance men like Zhu Tao and Li Xilie, entrenched on frontier ramparts, should secretly rise in the capital district—how would you prepare against them?
translations.idiomatic: If men like Zhu Tao and Li Xilie, entrenched on the frontiers, should strike at the capital itself, what force would be left to meet them?

sentences.zh: 夫關中，王業根本在焉。

translations.literal: Guanzhong is where the royal enterprise has its root.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong is the root of the imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 豪傑之在關中者，與籍於營衛不殊；

translations.literal: The heroes in Guanzhong are no different from those registered in the camp guard;
translations.idiomatic: The able men of Guanzhong are as good as men already enrolled in the palace guard;

sentences.zh: 車乘之在關中者，與列於廄牧不殊；

translations.literal: the carriages and teams in Guanzhong are no different from those arrayed in the imperial stables;
translations.idiomatic: its horses and chariots are as good as those in the imperial stables;

sentences.zh: 財用之在關中者，與貯於帑藏不殊。

translations.literal: the wealth and resources in Guanzhong are no different from those stored in the treasury vaults.
translations.idiomatic: and its wealth is as good as wealth already stored in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 一朝有急，可取也。

translations.literal: If one morning there is urgency, they can be taken up.
translations.idiomatic: In an emergency they can be drawn on at once.

sentences.zh: 陛下幸聽臣計，使芃還軍援洛，懷光救襄城，希烈必走。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, if you will heed my plan—send Pi back with his army to aid Luoyang, let Huaiguang rescue Xiangcheng—and Xilie will surely flee.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will accept my plan—send Pi back to relieve Luoyang, let Huaiguang raise the siege of Xiangcheng—and Xilie will certainly retreat.

sentences.zh: 請神策軍及將家子占而東者追還之，凡京師稅間架、榷酒、抽貫、貸商、點召之令，一切停之，則端本整棼之術。

translations.literal: I ask that the Shence armies and the sons of general families impressed for the eastern campaign be recalled; and that all capital orders for the jianjia house tax, wine monopoly, commodity surtax, loans to merchants, and press-gang summons be halted entirely—this is the method of setting the root straight and ordering what is tangled.
translations.idiomatic: Recall the Shence armies and the sons of military families sent east; abolish every emergency levy in the capital—the house tax, wine monopoly, commodity surtax, forced loans to merchants, and press-gang summons. That is how to set the root straight and untangle the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not adopt his advice.

sentences.zh: 後涇師急變，贄言皆效。

translations.literal: Later, when the Jing army mutiny erupted, all of Zai's words proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Jingzhou troops mutinied, everything Zai had warned of came true.

sentences.zh: 從狩奉天，機務填總，遠近調發，奏請報下，書詔日數百，贄初若不經思，逮成，皆周盡事情，衍繹孰復，人人可曉。

translations.literal: He followed the hunt to Fengtian. State affairs piled up in total; near and far were mobilized, memorials and replies issued, edicts and proclamations numbering in the hundreds each day. Zai at first seemed not to ponder, but when finished each document thoroughly covered the matter, developed and reviewed with care, so that every man could understand.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Fengtian during the flight. Affairs of state piled up without pause: levies and dispatches from near and far, memorials answered, edicts issued by the hundred each day. Zai seemed to draft without effort, yet every finished text covered the matter fully, reasoned through with care, and clear to all who read it.

sentences.zh: 旁吏承寫不給，它學士筆閣不得下，而贄沛然有餘。

translations.literal: The clerks beside him could not keep up with copying; the other academicians' brushes stuck in the inkstone and could not descend, while Zai overflowed with surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Copyists could not keep pace; other academicians could not get their brushes to move, while Zai still had strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 始，帝倉卒變故，每自克責。

translations.literal: At first, after the sudden calamity, the emperor often blamed himself.
translations.idiomatic: At first, shaken by the sudden disaster, the emperor often blamed himself.

sentences.zh: 贄曰：「陛下引咎，堯、舜意也。

translations.literal: Zai said: "Your Majesty takes blame upon yourself—this is the mind of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Zai said, "Your Majesty's willingness to accept blame is worthy of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 然致寇者乃群臣罪。」

translations.literal: Yet those who brought the invaders are the crime of the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: But it was your ministers who brought the invaders upon you.

sentences.zh: 贄意指盧杞等。

translations.literal: Zai's meaning pointed at Lu Qi and others.
translations.idiomatic: He had Lu Qi and his circle in mind.

sentences.zh: 帝護杞，因曰：「卿不忍歸過朕，有是言哉。

translations.literal: The emperor shielded Qi and therefore said: "You cannot bear to lay the fault on me and so speak thus.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor protected Qi and replied, "You cannot bear to lay the blame on me, and so you say this.

sentences.zh: 然自古興衰，其亦有天命乎？

translations.literal: Yet since antiquity rise and fall—does it also have the Mandate of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Yet since antiquity, has the rise and fall of dynasties not also depended on Heaven's mandate?

sentences.zh: 今之厄運，恐不在人也。」

translations.literal: Today's hard fate—perhaps it is not in men.
translations.idiomatic: Today's calamity may lie beyond human agency.

sentences.zh: 贄退而上書曰：

translations.literal: Zai withdrew and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zai withdrew and submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 自安史之亂，朝廷因循涵養，而諸方自擅壤地，未嘗會朝。

translations.literal: Since the An-Shi rebellion the court has followed old ways and nourished forbearance, while the various regions have monopolized their own territories and have not come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Since the An Lushan rebellion the court has been indulgent and passive, while the regions have held their own ground and seldom attended court.

sentences.zh: 陛下將一區宇，乃命將興師，以討四方。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wished to unify the realm and therefore ordered generals to raise armies to chastise the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty sought to reunify the realm, you ordered generals to raise armies against every quarter.

sentences.zh: 一人征行，十室資奉；

translations.literal: When one man goes on campaign, ten households supply him;
translations.idiomatic: One man sent to war was supported by ten households;

sentences.zh: 居者疲饋轉，行者苦鋒鏑；

translations.literal: those who stayed were worn out by transport and supply, those who marched suffered under blades and arrows;
translations.idiomatic: those who stayed behind were exhausted by transport levies, those who marched suffered under arms;

sentences.zh: 去留騷然，而閭裏不寧矣。

translations.literal: whether departing or remaining, all were in turmoil, and the hamlets and lanes knew no peace.
translations.idiomatic: communities were thrown into turmoil, and the countryside knew no peace.

sentences.zh: 聚兵日眾，供費日博，常賦不給，乃議蹙限而加斂焉；

translations.literal: As armies gathered daily in greater numbers and expenses daily swelled, regular levies could not suffice, and so they debated tightening quotas and adding collections;
translations.idiomatic: As armies grew and costs mounted, regular taxes no longer sufficed, and officials debated tightening quotas and adding new levies;

sentences.zh: 加斂既殫，乃別配之；

translations.literal: when added collections were exhausted, they then made separate allocations;
translations.idiomatic: when those additions were exhausted, separate assessments followed;

sentences.zh: 別配不足，於是榷算之科設，率貸之法興。

translations.literal: when separate allocations were insufficient, then monopoly and assessment categories were established and forced-loan methods arose.
translations.idiomatic: when even those failed, monopoly taxes and forced loans were imposed.

sentences.zh: 禁防滋章，吏不堪命；

translations.literal: Prohibitions and controls multiplied in number; officials could not bear the commands;
translations.idiomatic: Regulations multiplied until officials could not endure their duties;

sentences.zh: 農桑廢於追呼，膏血竭於笞捶；

translations.literal: farming and sericulture were abandoned to pursuit and summons; life's fat and blood were drained by flogging;
translations.idiomatic: farming was abandoned to tax collectors, and people's substance was drained by the lash;

sentences.zh: 兆庶嗷然，而郡邑不寧矣。

translations.literal: the myriad people cried out, and the commanderies and districts knew no peace.
translations.idiomatic: the common people cried out in distress, and the provinces were left in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 邊陲之戍以保封疆，禁衛之旅以備巡警，邦之大防也。

translations.literal: Frontier garrisons protect the borders; palace guard brigades prepare for patrol and alarm—the great defenses of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrisons guard the borders; palace guards stand ready for patrol and alarm—the great defenses of the state.

sentences.zh: 陛下悉而東征，邊備空屈，又搜私牧、責將家以出兵籍馬。

translations.literal: Your Majesty sent them all east to campaign; frontier defenses were emptied and strained, and private studs were searched while general families were charged to supply registered horses for the army.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sent them all east, leaving the frontiers bare, then seized private studs and pressed the sons of military families to furnish horses from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 夫私牧者，元勛貴戚之門也；

translations.literal: Private studs belong to the households of founding ministers and noble kin;
translations.idiomatic: Private studs belonged to the households of founding ministers and imperial kin;

sentences.zh: 將家者，統帥嶽牧之後也；

translations.literal: general families are the descendants of commanders and frontier governors;
translations.idiomatic: military families were the descendants of frontier commanders;

sentences.zh: 其復除征徭舊矣。

translations.literal: their exemptions from corvée and levies are of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: their exemptions from corvée and tax had long been established.

sentences.zh: 今奪其畜牧，事其子孫，丐假以給資裝，破產以營卒乘，元臣貴位，孰不解體？

translations.literal: Now you seize their livestock, employ their sons and grandsons, force them to beg and borrow to supply equipment, and ruin their estates to outfit soldiers and chariots—among founding ministers and noble rank, who would not be disheartened?
translations.idiomatic: Now their herds were seized, their sons conscripted, their families forced to borrow for equipment and ruined to outfit troops—who among the great ministers and nobles would not have been broken in spirit?

sentences.zh: 方且稅侯王之廬，算裨販之緡，貴不見優，近不見異，群情囂然而關畿不寧矣。

translations.literal: At the same time you taxed the dwellings of marquises and kings and assessed the cash of petty traders; the noble saw no favor, the near saw no distinction—and popular feeling grew clamorous while the capital region knew no peace.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the dwellings of princes were taxed and petty traders assessed; the great received no favor, the humble no relief—and popular anger rose until the capital itself was unsettled.

sentences.zh: 陛下又謂百度弛廢，則持義以掩恩，任法以成治，斷失於太速，察傷於太精。

translations.literal: Your Majesty also said that the hundred offices had grown lax and abandoned duty, and therefore upheld righteousness to cover kindness and relied on law to complete governance—yet judgment erred in being too swift and scrutiny harmed in being too fine.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty also believed that government had grown lax, and so upheld righteousness to mask kindness and relied on law to restore order—yet judgments were made too swiftly and scrutiny was carried too far.

sentences.zh: 斷速則寡恕於人，而疑似不容辨也；

translations.literal: When judgment is swift, there is little forgiveness toward men, and what is doubtful or merely suspected is not allowed to be distinguished;
translations.idiomatic: Swift judgment left little room for mercy, and the merely suspected were not given a hearing;

sentences.zh: 察精則多猜於物，而億度未必然也。

translations.literal: when scrutiny is fine, there is much suspicion of things, and surmise is not necessarily so.
translations.idiomatic: excessive scrutiny bred suspicion where surmise was not proof.

sentences.zh: 寡恕而下懼禍，故反側之釁生；

translations.literal: With little forgiveness, those below fear calamity, and thus the omen of turning and tossing arises;
translations.idiomatic: With little forgiveness below, men feared disaster, and unrest followed;

sentences.zh: 多猜而下防嫌，故茍且之患作。

translations.literal: with much suspicion, those below guard against resentment, and thus the affliction of mere expediency appears.
translations.idiomatic: with much suspicion below, men guarded against blame, and petty evasions multiplied.

sentences.zh: 由是叛亂繼產，忿讟並興，非常之虞，惟人主獨不聞。

translations.literal: From this rebellions followed one after another, anger and complaint rose together, and extraordinary anxieties—only the ruler alone did not hear of them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellions followed in succession, anger and complaint spread together, and extraordinary dangers arose—yet the throne alone heard nothing of them.

sentences.zh: 兇卒鼓行，白晝犯闕；

translations.literal: Ferocious soldiers beat the drums and marched; in broad daylight they violated the palace;
translations.idiomatic: Mutinous soldiers marched in formation and breached the palace in broad daylight;

sentences.zh: 重門無結草之禦，環衛無誰何之人。

translations.literal: the layered gates had no defense of tied grass, and the encircling guard had no one to challenge the intruders.
translations.idiomatic: the layered gates offered no defense, and the palace guard had no one to stop them.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖有股肱之臣，耳目之佐，見危不能竭誠，臨難不能效死，是則群臣之罪也。

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty had ministers as arms and legs and assistants as eyes and ears, seeing danger they could not exhaust their loyalty, facing hardship they could not offer their lives in service—this is the crime of the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty had ministers as arms and eyes as ears, they could not give their full loyalty in danger or their lives in crisis—that is the ministers' fault.

sentences.zh: 陛下方以興衰諉之天命，亦過矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now attributing rise and fall to the Mandate of Heaven—this too is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: For Your Majesty now to attribute rise and fall to Heaven's mandate alone is to go too far.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「天視自我民視，天聽自我民聽。」

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Heaven sees as my people see; Heaven hears as my people hear.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "Heaven sees through the eyes of the people; Heaven hears through the ears of the people.

sentences.zh: 則天所視聽，皆因於人，非人事外自有天命也。

translations.literal: Thus what Heaven sees and hears all depends on men; apart from human affairs there is no Mandate of Heaven on its own.
translations.idiomatic: What Heaven sees and hears therefore depends on human affairs; there is no mandate apart from how men govern.

sentences.zh: 紂之辭曰：「我生不有命在天？」

translations.literal: Zhou's words were: "Was I not born with mandate in Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou said, "Was I not born with Heaven's mandate?

sentences.zh: 此舍人事推天命，必不可之理也。

translations.literal: This abandons human affairs and pushes responsibility onto the Mandate of Heaven—a principle that surely cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: That is to abandon human responsibility and appeal to Heaven—a course that cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「自天祐之。」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Heaven assists him.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "Heaven assists him.

sentences.zh: 仲尼以謂：「祐者助也。

translations.literal: Confucius said of this: "To assist means to help.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius explained, "To assist means to help.

sentences.zh: 天之所助者順也，人之所助者信也。

translations.literal: What Heaven assists is compliance; what men assist is trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven assists those who follow the Way; men assist those who keep faith.

sentences.zh: 履信思乎順，是以祐之。」

translations.literal: To practice trust and think of compliance—therefore Heaven assists him."
translations.idiomatic: Practice faith and act in accord with the Way, and Heaven will assist you."

sentences.zh: 《易》論天人祐助之際，必先履行，而吉兇之報象焉。

translations.literal: The Changes discusses the juncture of Heaven and man and assistance: one must first practice conduct, and the omens of fortune and misfortune respond accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In discussing how Heaven and man assist one another, the Changes insists that conduct must come first; only then do the signs of fortune or misfortune appear.

sentences.zh: 此天命在人，蓋昭昭矣。

translations.literal: That the Mandate of Heaven lies in men is quite plainly clear.
translations.idiomatic: That Heaven's mandate rests in human affairs could hardly be clearer.

sentences.zh: 人事治而天降亂，未之有也；

translations.literal: When human affairs are well governed and Heaven sends chaos—never has this been;
translations.idiomatic: When human affairs are well ordered yet Heaven sends chaos—there has never been such a thing;

sentences.zh: 人事亂而天降康，亦未之有也。

translations.literal: when human affairs are chaotic and Heaven sends peace—never has this been either.
translations.idiomatic: when human affairs are in disorder yet Heaven sends peace—there has never been such a thing either.

sentences.zh: 尚恐有可疑者，請以近事信之。

translations.literal: If you still fear there may be doubt, please let recent events confirm it.
translations.idiomatic: If doubt remains, let recent events prove the point.

sentences.zh: 自比兵興，物力耗竭。

translations.literal: Since the recent rise of warfare, material resources have been exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Since warfare began, material resources have been exhausted.

sentences.zh: 人心驚疑如風濤然，洶洶靡定，族謀聚議，謂必有變。

translations.literal: Hearts were alarmed and doubtful like wind and waves, surging without rest; clans plotted and gathered in counsel, saying that change was certain.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts surged with alarm like wind-driven waves, never settling; families met in counsel, convinced that upheaval was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 則京師之人，固非悉通占術、曉天命也，則致寇之由，豈運當然？

translations.literal: Then the people of the capital—surely not all versed in divination and versed in Heaven's mandate—so the cause of bringing invaders: how could it be that fortune ordained it?
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital are not all versed in divination or Heaven's mandate—so how could the coming of invaders have been ordained by fate alone?

sentences.zh: 夫治或生亂，亂或資治；

translations.literal: Governance may give birth to chaos, and chaos may supply governance;
translations.idiomatic: Order can breed disorder, and disorder can supply the means to restore order;

sentences.zh: 有以無難而亡，多難而興。

translations.literal: some perish without difficulty, and many difficulties give rise to flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: some states fall though untroubled, while many rise through hardship.

sentences.zh: 治或生亂者，恃治而不修也；

translations.literal: When governance gives birth to chaos, it is because one relies on governance and does not cultivate;
translations.idiomatic: When order breeds disorder, it is because rulers trust in peace and neglect cultivation;

sentences.zh: 亂或資治者，遭亂而能治也；

translations.literal: when chaos supplies governance, it is because one meets chaos and is able to govern;
translations.idiomatic: when disorder supplies order, it is because rulers meet crisis and govern well;

sentences.zh: 無難而失者，忽萬幾之重，而忘憂畏也；

translations.literal: when one loses without difficulty, it is because one neglects the weight of ten thousand affairs and forgets worry and fear;
translations.idiomatic: when a state falls though untroubled, it is because the ruler neglects the weight of affairs and forgets caution;

sentences.zh: 多難而興者，涉庶事之艱，而知敕慎也。

translations.literal: when many difficulties give rise to flourishing, it is because one passes through the hardships of myriad affairs and knows vigilance and care.
translations.idiomatic: when a state rises through hardship, it is because the ruler has endured trial and learned vigilance.

sentences.zh: 今生亂失序之事不可追矣，其資治興邦之業，在刻勵而謹修之。

translations.literal: Now the matter of giving birth to chaos and losing order cannot be pursued back; the enterprise of supplying governance and raising the state lies in earnest effort and careful cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: The disorders of the past cannot be undone; what remains is the work of restoring order through earnest discipline and careful government.

sentences.zh: 當至危之機，得其道則興，失則廢，其間不容復有所悔也，惟勤思而熟計之。

translations.literal: At a moment of utmost peril, if one obtains the Way one flourishes, if one loses it one is ruined—between these there is no room for further regret; only diligent thought and thorough planning.
translations.idiomatic: At a moment of utmost peril, gain the Way and the dynasty revives; lose it and the dynasty perishes—there is no room left for regret, only for diligent thought and thorough planning.

sentences.zh: 舍己以從眾，違欲以遵道，遠憸佞，親忠直，推至誠，去逆詐，斯道甚易知，甚易行，不耗神，不劬力，第約之於心耳。

translations.literal: Set aside oneself to follow the multitude, set aside desires to follow the Way, keep the sycophantic and fawning at a distance, draw the loyal and upright near, extend utmost sincerity, remove perverse deceit—this Way is very easy to know, very easy to practice, consumes no spirit, demands no strenuous effort; it needs only to be bound to the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Set self aside to follow the people, set desire aside to follow the Way, keep sycophants at a distance and draw the loyal near, extend utmost sincerity and cast off deceit—the Way is easy to know and easy to practice, costing neither spirit nor strength, needing only to be held in the heart.

sentences.zh: 何憂乎亂人，何畏乎厄運，何患乎不寧哉？

translations.literal: Why worry about disorderly men, why fear hard fate, why dread lack of peace?
translations.idiomatic: Why then fear rebellious men, hard fortune, or unrest?

sentences.zh: 帝又問贄事切於今者，贄勸帝：「群臣參日，使極言得失。

translations.literal: The emperor again asked Zai about matters urgent for the present. Zai urged the emperor: "Let the ministers attend daily and speak to the utmost of gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again asked what was most urgent for the present. Zai urged him: "Let your ministers attend daily and speak freely of what is right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 若以軍務對者，見不以時，聽納無倦。

translations.literal: If they respond on military affairs, receive them not at fixed times and listen without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: If they speak on military affairs, receive them without fixed schedules and listen without weariness.

sentences.zh: 兼天下之智以為聰明。」

translations.literal: Take the wisdom of all under Heaven as your own clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Take the wisdom of the whole realm as your own intelligence.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕豈不推誠！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do I not extend sincerity!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Do I not extend sincerity!

sentences.zh: 然顧上封者，惟譏斥人短長，類非忠直。

translations.literal: Yet those who submit sealed memorials only ridicule and expose men's faults and merits—mostly not loyal and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who submit sealed memorials mostly attack others' faults—hardly the voice of loyal integrity.

sentences.zh: 往謂君臣一體，故推信不疑，至憸人賣為威福。

translations.literal: Formerly I said ruler and minister are one body, and therefore extended trust without doubt—until the fawning sold authority for power and favor.
translations.idiomatic: I once held that ruler and minister were one body and trusted without reserve—until sycophants traded authority for power.

sentences.zh: 今茲之禍，推誠之敝也。

translations.literal: Today's calamity is the defect of extending trust.
translations.idiomatic: Today's calamity is the price of that unchecked trust.

sentences.zh: 又諫者不密，要須歸曲於朕，以自取名。

translations.literal: Moreover remonstrators are not discreet; they must twist the blame back to me to make a name for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: And remonstrators are indiscreet; they twist blame back onto me to win a name for themselves.

sentences.zh: 朕嗣位，見言事多矣，大抵雷同道聽，加質則窮。

translations.literal: Since I succeeded to the throne I have seen many who speak on affairs; mostly they echo one another and follow hearsay—add questioning and they are cornered.
translations.idiomatic: Since my accession I have heard countless memorials; most echo one another and follow rumor—question them closely and they are exposed.

sentences.zh: 故頃不詔次對，豈曰倦哉！」

translations.literal: Therefore recently I have not ordered ranked responses—is that weariness!
translations.idiomatic: That is why I recently stopped ordered responses to memorials—not from weariness!

sentences.zh: 贄因是極諫曰：

translations.literal: Zai therefore remonstrated to the utmost, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zai thereupon remonstrated forcefully:

sentences.zh: 昔人有因噎而廢食者，又有懼溺而自沈者，其為防患，不亦過哉！

translations.literal: In old times there was one who, because he choked, abandoned eating, and another who, fearing drowning, drowned himself—their precaution against harm was not excessive!
translations.idiomatic: There were men who stopped eating because they once choked, and men who drowned themselves for fear of water—such caution against harm goes too far!

sentences.zh: 願陛下鑒之，毋以小虞而妨大道也。

translations.literal: I ask Your Majesty to take this as a mirror and not let small anxieties obstruct the great Way.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to take this as a warning and not let small fears obstruct the great Way.

sentences.zh: 臣聞人之所助在信，信之所本在誠。

translations.literal: I have heard that what men assist is trust, and what trust rests on is sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: What men will assist is trust, and trust rests on sincerity.

sentences.zh: 一不誠，心莫之保；

translations.literal: With one lack of sincerity, the heart cannot be secured;
translations.idiomatic: Without sincerity, the heart cannot be secured;

sentences.zh: 一不信，言莫之行。

translations.literal: with one lack of trust, words cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: without trust, words cannot be acted upon.

sentences.zh: 故聖人重焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages valued these.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sages prized them.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「誠者，物之終始，不誠無物。」

translations.literal: The tradition says: "Sincerity is the end and beginning of things; without sincerity there are no things.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says, "Sincerity is the beginning and end of all things; without sincerity nothing is accomplished.

sentences.zh: 物者事也，言不誠即無所事矣。

translations.literal: Things means affairs; if words are not sincere, then nothing is done.
translations.idiomatic: Things means affairs; without sincerity in speech, nothing is done.

sentences.zh: 匹夫不誠，無復有事，況王者賴人之誠以自固，而可不誠於人乎？

translations.literal: If a common man is not sincere, he has nothing more to do—how much more must a king, who relies on men's sincerity to secure himself, be sincere toward men!
translations.idiomatic: If an ordinary man without sincerity accomplishes nothing, how much more must a king, who depends on others' sincerity to stand firm, be sincere toward his people!

sentences.zh: 陛下所謂誠信以致害者，臣竊非之。

translations.literal: What Your Majesty calls sincerity and trust bringing harm—I privately do not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds that sincerity and trust brought harm—I cannot agree.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「可與言而不與之言，失人；

translations.literal: Confucius said: "With one who may be spoken to, not to speak is to lose the man;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Not to speak to one who may be spoken to is to lose the man;

sentences.zh: 不可與言而與之言，失言。

translations.literal: with one who may not be spoken to, to speak is to lose the words.
translations.idiomatic: to speak to one who may not be spoken to is to lose the words.

sentences.zh: 智者不失人，亦不失言。」

translations.literal: The wise man loses neither man nor words.
translations.idiomatic: The wise lose neither man nor words.

sentences.zh: 陛下可審其言而不可不信，可慎其所與而不可不誠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty may examine their words and cannot but trust; may be careful whom you associate with and cannot but be sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may test their words without ceasing to trust, and choose your associates carefully without ceasing to be sincere.

sentences.zh: 所謂民者，至愚而神。

translations.literal: What are called the people are most foolish yet most spirit-like.
translations.idiomatic: The people are at once most foolish and most spirit-like.

sentences.zh: 夫蚩蚩之倫，或昏或鄙，此似於愚也。

translations.literal: Those common folk—some dull, some crude—this seems like foolishness.
translations.idiomatic: The common multitude may seem dull or crude—that appears foolish.

sentences.zh: 然上之得失靡不辨，好惡靡不知，所秘靡不傳，所為靡不效。

translations.literal: Yet the ruler's gains and losses they all distinguish, likes and dislikes they all know; what is secret they all transmit, what is done they all effect.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they distinguish the ruler's every gain and loss, know every like and dislike, spread every secret, and echo every act.

sentences.zh: 馭以智則詐，示以疑則偷；

translations.literal: Govern them with cunning and they deceive; show them suspicion and they steal;
translations.idiomatic: Rule them with cunning and they deceive; show them suspicion and they evade;

sentences.zh: 接不以禮則其徇義輕，撫不以情則其效忠薄。

translations.literal: receive them without ritual and their devotion to righteousness is light; comfort them without feeling and their loyalty in service is thin.
translations.idiomatic: receive them without courtesy and their sense of duty grows light; comfort them without warmth and their loyalty grows thin.

sentences.zh: 上行則下從之，上施則下報之，若景附形，若響應聲。

translations.literal: When the ruler acts, those below follow; when the ruler bestows, those below repay—like shadow following form, like echo answering sound.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler acts, the people follow; when the ruler bestows, the people repay—like shadow to form, like echo to sound.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「惟天下至誠，為能盡其性。」

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "Only under Heaven utmost sincerity can fully realize one's nature.
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said, "Only the utmost sincerity under Heaven can fully realize one's nature.

sentences.zh: 不盡於己而責盡於人，不誠於前而望誠於後，必紿而不信矣。

translations.literal: Not exhausting oneself yet demanding exhaustion from others, not sincere before yet expecting sincerity after—surely deception and no trust.
translations.idiomatic: To demand fullness from others without fulfilling oneself, to expect sincerity afterward without being sincere before—can only breed deceit, not trust.

sentences.zh: 今方鎮有不誠於國，陛下興師伐之；

translations.literal: Now if a frontier commander is not sincere toward the state, Your Majesty raises armies to chastise him;
translations.idiomatic: When a frontier commander is disloyal to the state, Your Majesty sends armies against him;

sentences.zh: 臣有不信於上，陛下下令誅之。

translations.literal: if a minister is not trustworthy toward the ruler, Your Majesty issues orders to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: when a minister is untrustworthy to the throne, Your Majesty orders his execution.

sentences.zh: 有司奉命而不敢赦者，以陛下所有責彼所無也。

translations.literal: The officials carry out the command and dare not pardon—because Your Majesty possesses what they lack.
translations.idiomatic: Officials obey without daring to pardon—because Your Majesty holds what they lack.

sentences.zh: 故誠與信不可斯須去己。

translations.literal: Therefore sincerity and trust cannot for an instant be removed from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity and trust cannot for an instant be set aside.

sentences.zh: 願陛下慎守而力行之，恐非所以為悔也。

translations.literal: I ask Your Majesty to guard them carefully and practice them with force—then I fear there will be no cause for regret.
translations.idiomatic: Guard them carefully and practice them steadfastly—then there will be no cause for regret.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「人誰無過？

translations.literal: The tradition says: "Who among men has no faults?
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says, "Who among men is without fault?

sentences.zh: 過而能改，善莫大焉。」

translations.literal: To have faults and be able to reform—nothing is greater in goodness.
translations.idiomatic: To err and reform—nothing is greater in goodness.

sentences.zh: 仲虺歌成湯之德曰：「改過不吝。」

translations.literal: Zhong Hui sang the virtue of King Cheng of Tang: "To reform faults without stinginess."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui praised King Tang's virtue: "He reformed faults without reluctance."

sentences.zh: 吉甫美宣王之功曰：「袞職有闕，仲山甫補之。」

translations.literal: Jifu praised King Xuan's achievement: "The kingly duties had gaps; Zhong Shanfu mended them."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu praised King Xuan: "Where the royal duties had gaps, Zhong Shanfu filled them."

sentences.zh: 夫成湯聖君也，仲虺聖輔也，以聖輔贊聖君，不稱其無過，稱其改過；

translations.literal: Cheng Tang was a sage king, Zhong Hui a sage assistant; with a sage assistant aiding a sage king, he did not praise him for having no faults but praised him for reforming faults;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tang was a sage king and Zhong Hui a sage minister; the sage minister did not praise his king for being without fault, but for reforming fault;

sentences.zh: 周宣中興賢王也，吉甫文武賢臣也，歌誦其主，不美其無闕，而美其補闕。

translations.literal: King Xuan of Zhou was a worthy king in restoration, Jifu a worthy minister in civil and military affairs; singing praise of his lord, he did not beautify him for having no gaps but beautified him for mending gaps.
translations.idiomatic: King Xuan restored Zhou and Jifu was his worthy minister; in praising his lord he did not glorify him for having no flaws, but for mending flaws.

sentences.zh: 則聖賢之意，貴於改過，較然甚明。

translations.literal: Then the meaning of sage and worthy is to value reforming faults—comparatively very clear.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson of sage and worthy is plain: to reform fault is what matters.

sentences.zh: 蓋過差者，上智下愚所不免，惟智者能改而之善，愚者恥而之非也。

translations.literal: Faults and errors are what the highest wisdom and lowest foolishness alike cannot avoid; only the wise can reform them toward good, while the foolish are ashamed and turn them toward wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Faults are unavoidable to sage and fool alike; the wise reform toward good, the foolish are ashamed and turn toward wrong.

sentences.zh: 中古以降，其臣尚諛，其君亦自聖，掩盛德，行小道，乃有入則造膝，出則詭辭，奸由此滋，善由此沮，天子意由此惑，爭臣罪由此生，媚道行而害斯甚矣。

translations.literal: From middle antiquity downward, ministers still flattered and rulers also deemed themselves sage, covering great virtue and practicing petty ways—then there were those who on entering made knees and on leaving spoke crooked words; from this flattery grew, from this goodness was obstructed, from this the Son of Heaven's mind was confused, from this the crime of contentious ministers arose, and when the way of fawning ran, the harm was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Since middle antiquity ministers have flattered and rulers deemed themselves sage, hiding great virtue and practicing petty ways—entering to whisper at the knee, leaving to speak crookedly; flattery grew, goodness was blocked, the Son of Heaven was confused, and the harm of sycophancy became extreme.

sentences.zh: 太宗有文武仁義之德、治致太平之功，可謂盛矣，然而人到於今以從諫改過為稱首。

translations.literal: Taizong had the virtue of civil, military, benevolence, and righteousness and the achievement of governing to great peace—he may be called flourishing; yet men to this day take following remonstrance and reforming faults as his foremost praise.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had civil and military virtue and brought great peace—yet men to this day praise him most for accepting remonstrance and reforming fault.

sentences.zh: 是知諫而能從，過而能改，帝王之大烈也。

translations.literal: Thus to remonstrate and be able to follow, to have faults and be able to reform—these are the great achievements of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: To accept remonstrance and reform fault is the great achievement of kings.

sentences.zh: 陛下謂諫官論事，引善自予，歸過於上者，信非其美，然於盛德，未有虧焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty says remonstrating officials discuss affairs by citing good to oneself and attributing fault to the ruler—truly not their beauty; yet toward great virtue there is no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty says remonstrators claim credit for good and lay blame on the throne—that is not admirable; yet it does not diminish your great virtue.

sentences.zh: 納而不違，傳之適足增美；

translations.literal: Accept and do not oppose—transmission of it only adds beauty;
translations.idiomatic: Accept without resisting, and the story only adds to your glory;

sentences.zh: 拒而違之，又安能禁之勿傳？

translations.literal: reject and oppose—how can you forbid it from being transmitted?
translations.idiomatic: reject and resist, and how can you stop it from spreading?

sentences.zh: 不宜以此梗進言之路也。

translations.literal: One should not use this to block the road of advancing speech.
translations.idiomatic: Do not use this to block the path of frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 聖人不忽細微，不侮鰥寡；

translations.literal: Sages do not neglect the minute, do not insult widowers and widows;
translations.idiomatic: Sages do not neglect the small, do not despise the weak;

sentences.zh: 奓言無驗不必用，質言當理不必違；

translations.literal: extravagant words without verification need not be used, plain words that accord with reason need not be opposed;
translations.idiomatic: extravagant words without proof need not be followed, plain words that accord with reason need not be rejected;

sentences.zh: 遜於誌不必然，逆於心不必否；

translations.literal: words agreeable to one's intent are not necessarily so, words contrary to one's heart are not necessarily wrong;
translations.idiomatic: words that please one's intent are not necessarily right, words that offend one's heart are not necessarily wrong;

sentences.zh: 異於人不必是，同於眾不必非；

translations.literal: words unlike others' need not be correct, words like the multitude's need not be wrong;
translations.idiomatic: words unlike others need not be right, words like the crowd need not be wrong;

sentences.zh: 辭拙而效迂者不必愚，言甘而利重者不必智。

translations.literal: clumsy words with remote effect need not be foolish, sweet words with heavy profit need not be wise.
translations.idiomatic: clumsy words with slow effect need not be foolish, sweet words with heavy gain need not be wise.

sentences.zh: 考之以實，惟善所在，則可以盡天下之心矣。

translations.literal: Test them by fact, follow wherever goodness lies—then one can exhaust the hearts of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Test by results and follow wherever goodness lies—then you can win the hearts of all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 夫人情蔽於所信，沮於所疑，忽於所輕，溺於所欲。

translations.literal: Human feeling is obscured by what one trusts, obstructed by what one doubts, neglects what one treats lightly, drowned in what one desires.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature is blinded by trust, blocked by doubt, neglects what is treated lightly, and is drowned by desire.

sentences.zh: 信偏則聽言不盡其實，故有過當之言；

translations.literal: When trust is partial, one hears words without exhausting their reality, and therefore there are words beyond measure;
translations.idiomatic: Partial trust hears words without testing them, and so exaggeration arises;

sentences.zh: 疑甚則雖實不聽其言，故有失實之聽。

translations.literal: when doubt is extreme, even true words are not heard, and therefore there is listening that loses reality.
translations.idiomatic: extreme doubt refuses even true words, and so judgment loses reality.

sentences.zh: 輕其人則遺可重之事，欲其事則存可棄之人。

translations.literal: Treat a man lightly and important affairs are abandoned; desire an affair and men who may be discarded are kept.
translations.idiomatic: Treat a man lightly and weighty affairs are lost; desire an outcome and men who should be dismissed are kept.

sentences.zh: 茍縱所私，不考其實，則是失天下之心矣。

translations.literal: If one indulges private inclination and does not test by fact, then one loses the hearts of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Indulge private feeling without testing by fact, and you lose the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 故常情之所輕，聖人之所重，不必慕高而好異也。

translations.literal: What common feeling treats lightly, the sage treats heavily—one need not admire the lofty and love the strange.
translations.idiomatic: What common feeling despises, the sage esteems—you need not chase the lofty and the strange.

sentences.zh: 陛下又以雷同道說，加質則窮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty also says they echo one another and follow hearsay—add questioning and they are cornered.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty also says they echo one another and follow rumor—question them and they are exposed.

sentences.zh: 臣謂陛下雖窮其辭而未窮其理，能服其口而未服其心。

translations.literal: I say Your Majesty may have exhausted their words but not exhausted their principle, may have won their mouths but not won their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may have exhausted their words but not their reasoning, won their mouths but not their hearts.

sentences.zh: 且下之情莫不願達於上，上之情莫不求知於下。

translations.literal: Moreover, those below all wish to reach those above; those above all seek to know those below.
translations.idiomatic: Those below all wish to reach the throne; the throne all seeks to know those below.

sentences.zh: 然而下常苦上之難達，上常苦下之難知。

translations.literal: Yet those below constantly suffer that those above are hard to reach; those above constantly suffer that those below are hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those below suffer that the throne is hard to reach, and the throne suffers that those below are hard to know.

sentences.zh: 若是者何？

translations.literal: If so, why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 九弊不去也。

translations.literal: Nine defects have not been removed.
translations.idiomatic: Because nine defects remain.

sentences.zh: 所謂九弊者，上有六，下有三：好勝人，恥聞過，騁辯給，衒聰明，厲威嚴，恣強愎，上之弊也；

translations.literal: What are called the nine defects: above there are six, below there are three—loving to overcome others, being ashamed to hear of faults, displaying eloquence, showing off intelligence, enforcing awe and severity, indulging strength and obstinacy—these are the defects above;
translations.idiomatic: The nine defects are six above and three below: loving to overcome others, shaming to hear fault, displaying eloquence, showing off intelligence, enforcing severity, indulging obstinacy—the defects of the ruler;

sentences.zh: 諂諛、顧望、畏懦，下之弊也。

translations.literal: flattery, looking back in hesitation, timid fear—these are the defects below.
translations.idiomatic: flattery, hesitation, and timid fear—the defects of ministers.

sentences.zh: 好勝而恥過，必甘佞辭，忌直言，則諂諛者進，而忠實之語不聞矣。

translations.literal: Loving to overcome and being ashamed of fault—one must relish fawning words, hate straight speech; then flatterers advance and loyal, honest words are not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Love of victory and shame at fault breed relish for flattery and hatred of straight speech—flatterers advance and loyal words are not heard.

sentences.zh: 騁辯而炫明，必折人以言，虞人以詐，則顧望者自便，而切摩之益不盡矣。

translations.literal: Displaying eloquence and showing intelligence—one must break others by words and guard against others by deceit; then the hesitant find their convenience and the benefit of earnest counsel is not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Display of eloquence and intelligence breaks others with words and traps them with deceit—the hesitant take their ease and earnest counsel never fully reaches the throne.

sentences.zh: 厲威而恣愎，必不能降情接物，引咎在己，則畏懦者至，而情理之說不申矣。

translations.literal: Enforcing awe and indulging obstinacy—one cannot lower feeling to meet things and take blame on oneself; then the timid arrive and the exposition of reason and feeling is not made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Severity and obstinacy prevent lowering oneself to meet others and taking blame upon oneself—the timid prevail and reason never fully prevails.

sentences.zh: 人之難知，堯、舜所病，胡可以一酬一詰，而謂盡其能哉？

translations.literal: That men are hard to know—Yao and Shun were afflicted by this; how can one reward and question once and say their capacity is exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: That men are hard to know afflicted even Yao and Shun—how can one exchange a single question and answer and claim to know their full capacity?

sentences.zh: 夫欲治天下，而不務得人心，則天下固不治矣；

translations.literal: One who wishes to govern all under Heaven yet does not strive to win hearts—then all under Heaven is certainly not governed;
translations.idiomatic: One who would govern the realm without winning hearts will certainly not govern it;

sentences.zh: 務得人心，而不勤接下，則心固不得矣；

translations.literal: strives to win hearts yet does not diligently receive those below—then hearts are certainly not won;
translations.idiomatic: one who strives for hearts without diligently receiving those below will certainly not win them;

sentences.zh: 務接下而不辨君子小人，則下固不可接矣；

translations.literal: strives to receive those below yet does not distinguish gentleman from petty man—then those below certainly cannot be received;
translations.idiomatic: one who receives those below without distinguishing gentleman from petty man certainly cannot receive them well;

sentences.zh: 務辨君子小人，而惡直嗜諛，則君子小人固不可辨矣。

translations.literal: strives to distinguish gentleman from petty man yet hates the straight and loves flattery—then gentleman and petty man certainly cannot be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: one who tries to distinguish the worthy from the base yet hates straight speech and loves flattery will never tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 趨和求媚，人之甚利存焉；

translations.literal: Rushing to harmony and seeking favor—within this men's greatest profit lies;
translations.idiomatic: To curry favor and seek approval is where men's greatest profit lies;

sentences.zh: 犯顏冒禍，人之甚害存焉。

translations.literal: offending the countenance and braving calamity—within this men's greatest harm lies.
translations.idiomatic: to offend the throne and risk disaster is where men's greatest harm lies.

sentences.zh: 居上者易其言而以美利利之，猶懼忠告之不暨，況疏隔而猜忌者乎？

translations.literal: For one above, to alter his words and entice with fine profit—one still fears loyal counsel will not reach him; how much more when estranged and suspicious?
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler alters his words and tempts with profit, loyal counsel may still fail to reach him—how much more when he is distant and suspicious?

sentences.zh: 是時，賊未平，帝欲明年遂改元，而術家爭言數鐘百六，宜有所變，示天下復始。

translations.literal: At this time the rebels were not yet pacified. The emperor wished to change the era name the next year, while diviners contended that the cycle of one hundred and six had arrived and there should be change, showing all under Heaven a fresh beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were not yet subdued. The emperor wished to change the era name the following year, while diviners argued that the cycle of one hundred and six required change to show the realm a new beginning.

sentences.zh: 帝乃議更益大號。

translations.literal: The emperor then discussed adding an even greater title.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then discussed adding an even grander imperial title.

sentences.zh: 贄曰：「今乘輿播越，大憝未去，此人情向背、天意去就之隙。

translations.literal: Zai said: "Now the imperial carriage is in exile and the great enemy has not departed—this is the juncture of men's inclinations and Heaven's coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Zai said, "The throne is in exile and the great enemy has not been removed—this is the moment when hearts may turn and Heaven's favor may shift.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜痛自貶勵，不宜益美名以累謙德。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should sternly humble and encourage yourself; you should not add fine names to burden modest virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should humble yourself deeply, not add glorious titles that would burden your modest virtue.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言固善，然要當小有變革，為朕計之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are indeed good, yet there must be some small change—plan it for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your counsel is sound, yet some small change is still needed—plan it for me."

sentences.zh: 贄奏言：「古之人君，德合於天曰『皇』，合於地曰『帝』，合於人曰『王』，父天母地以養人治物得其宜者曰『天子』，皆大名也。

translations.literal: Zai memorialized: "The rulers of old whose virtue accorded with Heaven were called 'August,' whose virtue accorded with Earth were called 'Emperor,' whose virtue accorded with men were called 'King'; one who as father to Heaven and mother to Earth nourished men and governed things in their proper measure was called 'Son of Heaven'—all great names.
translations.idiomatic: Zai submitted: "Ancient rulers whose virtue matched Heaven were called August; those who matched Earth, Emperor; those who matched men, King; one who as Heaven's son and Earth's child nourished the people and governed things rightly was called Son of Heaven—all great names.

sentences.zh: 三代而上，所稱象其德，不敢有加焉。

translations.literal: Before the Three Dynasties, what they were called mirrored their virtue; they dared not add to it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Three Dynasties, titles mirrored virtue; none dared add to them.

sentences.zh: 至秦乃兼曰『皇帝』，流及後世昏僻之君，始有聖劉、天元之號。

translations.literal: Only under Qin were they combined as 'Emperor'; flowing down to benighted and perverse rulers of later ages, there began titles like Holy Liu and Celestial Origin.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Qin were they combined as Emperor; later benighted rulers invented titles like Holy Liu and Celestial Origin.

sentences.zh: 故人主重輕，不在稱謂，視德何如耳。

translations.literal: Thus whether a ruler is weighty or light lies not in designation but in viewing how his virtue is.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's weight lies not in titles but in his virtue.

sentences.zh: 若以時屯當有變革，不若引咎降名，以祗天戒。

translations.literal: If because the times are straitened there should be change, better to take blame and lower the name to respect Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: If change is needed in hard times, better to accept blame and lower your title to heed Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 且矯舊失，至明也；

translations.literal: Moreover to correct old errors is utmost clarity;
translations.idiomatic: To correct past errors is the height of clarity;

sentences.zh: 損虛飾，大知也。

translations.literal: to reduce empty ornament is great wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: to strip empty display is great wisdom.

sentences.zh: 寧與加冗號以受實患哉？」

translations.literal: Would you rather add redundant titles and receive real harm?"
translations.idiomatic: Would you add empty titles and suffer real harm?"

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 會興元赦令方具，帝以稿付贄，使商討其詳。

translations.literal: It happened that the Xingyuan amnesty edict was being prepared; the emperor gave the draft to Zai to discuss its details.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xingyuan amnesty edict was being drafted, the emperor gave the manuscript to Zai to refine.

sentences.zh: 贄知帝執德不固，困則思治，泰則易驕，欲激之使強其意，即建言：「履非常之危者，不可以常道安；

translations.literal: Zai knew the emperor's hold on virtue was not firm—in hardship he thought of order, in ease he easily grew proud—and wished to stir him to strengthen his resolve. He therefore advised: "One who treads extraordinary peril cannot be settled by ordinary ways;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor's virtue was not firm—reflective in hardship, proud in ease—Zai sought to strengthen his resolve and advised: "One in extraordinary peril cannot be settled by ordinary means;

sentences.zh: 解非常之紛者，不可以常令諭。

translations.literal: one who resolves extraordinary turmoil cannot be instructed by ordinary orders.
translations.idiomatic: one who resolves extraordinary turmoil cannot be governed by ordinary commands.

sentences.zh: 陛下窮用兵甲，竭取財賦，變生京師，盜據宮闥。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has exhausted arms and armor and drained taxes and levies; change arose in the capital and bandits seized the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has exhausted armies and drained the treasury; rebellion broke out in the capital and bandits seized the palace.

sentences.zh: 今假王者四兇，僭帝者二豎，其他顧瞻懷貳，不可悉數。

translations.literal: Now four fiends falsely claim kingship, two lads usurp the imperial title, and others who look about with divided hearts cannot all be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Four rebels falsely claim kingship, two usurpers claim the throne, and countless others waver in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 而欲紓多難，收群心，惟在赦令而已。

translations.literal: Yet to ease many hardships and gather all hearts depends solely on the amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: To ease hardship and win hearts depends solely on the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 動人以言，所感已淺；

translations.literal: To move men with words—the feeling aroused is already shallow;
translations.idiomatic: To move men with words already stirs them little;

sentences.zh: 言又不切，人誰肯懷？

translations.literal: if words are not earnest, who will embrace them?
translations.idiomatic: if words are not earnest, who will heed them?

sentences.zh: 故誠不至者物不感，損不極者益不臻。

translations.literal: Therefore where sincerity does not reach, things are not moved; where loss is not extreme, gain does not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Where sincerity does not reach, nothing moves; where repentance is not deep, no gain follows.

sentences.zh: 夫悔過不得不深，引咎不得不盡，招延不可不廣，潤澤不可不弘，使天下聞之，廓然一變，人人得其所欲，安有不服哉？

translations.literal: Repentance must be deep, taking blame must be complete, recruitment must be broad, grace must be expansive—let all under Heaven hear and be wholly transformed, each man obtaining what he desires; how could there be any who do not submit?
translations.idiomatic: Repentance must be deep, blame fully accepted, recruitment broad, grace expansive—let the realm hear and be transformed, each man receiving what he desires; who would not submit?

sentences.zh: 其須改革科條，已別封上。

translations.literal: The statutes needing reform have been submitted separately.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes needing reform have been submitted in a separate memorial.

sentences.zh: 臣聞知過非難，改之難；

translations.literal: I have heard that knowing fault is not hard, reforming it is hard;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing fault is not hard; reforming it is hard;

sentences.zh: 言善非難，行之難。

translations.literal: speaking good is not hard, practicing it is hard.
translations.idiomatic: speaking well is not hard; acting well is hard.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『聖人感人心而天下和平。』

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'The sage moves hearts and all under Heaven is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'The sage moves hearts and the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 夫感者，誠發於心而形於事，事或未諭，故宣之於言，言必顧心，心必副事，三者相合，乃可求感。

translations.literal: To move is for sincerity to issue from the heart and take form in affairs; when affairs are not yet understood, therefore one declares them in words. Words must look to the heart, the heart must match affairs—when the three accord, then one may seek to move.
translations.idiomatic: To move others, sincerity must issue from the heart and take form in action; when action is not understood, words declare it. Words must match the heart, the heart must match action—only when all three accord can hearts be moved.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下先斷厥誌，以施其辭，度可行者而宣之，不可者措之。

translations.literal: I ask Your Majesty first to decide your will, then apply your words; estimate what can be done and declare it, what cannot be done set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Decide your will first, then speak; declare what can be done and set aside what cannot.

sentences.zh: 無茍於言，以重取悔。」

translations.literal: Do not be careless in words and again incur regret.
translations.idiomatic: Do not speak carelessly and invite regret again.

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 始，帝播遷，府藏委棄，衛兵無褚衣。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor was driven into exile, treasury stores were abandoned and guard soldiers had no padded garments.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first fled, treasuries were abandoned and guards lacked padded clothing.

sentences.zh: 至是，天下貢奉稍至，乃於行在夾廡署瓊林、大盈二庫，別藏貢物。

translations.literal: By now tribute from all under Heaven gradually arrived, and at the temporary court they established Qionglín and Dayíng storehouses in the side corridors to store tribute goods separately.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute gradually arrived, and at the temporary court they established Qionglín and Dayíng storehouses in the side corridors for tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 贄諫，以為：「瓊林、大盈於古無傳。

translations.literal: Zai remonstrated, holding that: "Qionglín and Dayíng have no transmission in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Zai remonstrated: "Qionglín and Dayíng have no precedent in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 舊老皆言：開元時貴臣飾巧以求媚，建言郡邑賦稅，當委有司以制經用，其貢獻悉歸天子私有之。

translations.literal: Old men all say: In the Kaiyuan era noble ministers adorned craft to seek favor, advising that commandery and district taxes should be entrusted to officials to regulate regular use, while tribute should all return to the Son of Heaven's private possession.
translations.idiomatic: Elders say that in Kaiyuan favored ministers sought favor by advising that local taxes go to officials for public use while tribute became the emperor's private property.

sentences.zh: 蕩心侈欲，亦終以餌寇。

translations.literal: To unsettle the heart and indulge desire also in the end fed the invader.
translations.idiomatic: Indulgence in luxury ultimately fed the invaders.

sentences.zh: 今師旅方殷，瘡痛呻吟之聲未息，遽以珍貢私別庫，恐群下有所觖望，請悉出以賜有功。

translations.literal: Now armies are still pressing and the sound of wounds and groans has not ceased—suddenly to set aside precious tribute in private storehouses fears that those below will feel disappointment. I ask that all be distributed to reward the meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: Armies still press and the wounded still groan—to hoard tribute in private storehouses will disappoint your followers. Distribute all to reward merit.

sentences.zh: 令後納貢必歸之有司，先給軍賞，瑰怪纖麗無得以供。

translations.literal: Let future tribute necessarily return to the proper offices, first supplying military rewards; strange and fine trifles may not be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Let future tribute go to proper offices, first for military rewards; curios and finery should not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 是乃散小儲成大儲，捐小寶固大寶也。」

translations.literal: This is to scatter small stores to make a great store, to give small treasures to secure great treasure.
translations.idiomatic: This scatters small hoards to build a great hoard, gives small treasure to secure great treasure.

sentences.zh: 帝悟，即撤其署。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and immediately abolished the establishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and abolished the storehouses.

sentences.zh: 李懷光有異志，欲怒其軍使叛，即上言：「兵稟薄，與神策不等，難以戰。」

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang had a different intent and wished to anger his army into rebellion. He therefore submitted: "Army rations are thin and unequal to the Shence armies—hard to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang harbored rebellious intent and sought to provoke his troops. He submitted: "Our rations are thin and unequal to the Shence armies—we cannot fight.

sentences.zh: 李晟密言其變，因請移屯。

translations.literal: Li Sheng secretly reported his change and therefore asked to move camp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng secretly reported the plot and asked to move camp.

sentences.zh: 帝遣贄見懷光議事。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Zai to see Huaiguang to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zai to discuss matters with Huaiguang.

sentences.zh: 贄還奏：「懷光寇奔不追，師老不用，群帥欲進，輒沮止其謀。

translations.literal: Zai returned and reported: "Huaiguang did not pursue the fleeing bandits; his army was old and unused. When the commanders wished to advance, he always obstructed and stopped their plans.
translations.idiomatic: Zai reported: "Huaiguang did not pursue fleeing rebels; his army grew idle. Whenever commanders wished to advance, he blocked them.

sentences.zh: 此必反，宜有以制之。」

translations.literal: This man will surely rebel—there should be means to control him.
translations.idiomatic: He will surely rebel—we must restrain him.

sentences.zh: 因勸帝許晟移軍。

translations.literal: He therefore urged the emperor to permit Sheng to move his army.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to let Sheng move his army.

sentences.zh: 初，贄與懷光語及晟，懷光妄詫曰：「吾無所藉晟。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zai spoke with Huaiguang about Sheng, Huaiguang falsely boasted: "I have no need to rely on Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, speaking with Huaiguang of Sheng, Huaiguang boasted: "I need no help from Sheng.

sentences.zh: 贄即美其強雄，使不得翻覆。

translations.literal: Zai immediately praised his strength and heroism so that he could not turn about.
translations.idiomatic: Zai praised his strength so he would not change course.

sentences.zh: 至是，請下詔書如其意者，且無辭歸短於朝。
