translations.literal: On this occasion he asked that an edict be issued as Huaiguang wished, and that he not be allowed to return and speak ill of the court.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for an edict pleasing to Huaiguang, and that he not be allowed to malign the court on returning.

sentences.zh: 又建：「遣李建徽、陽惠元與晟並屯東渭橋，托言晟兵寡不足支賊，俾為掎角。

translations.literal: He also proposed: "Send Li Jianhui and Yang Huiyuan to camp with Sheng at East Wei Bridge, alleging that Sheng's troops were few and insufficient to support against the rebels, so that they might act as pincers.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed sending Li Jianhui and Yang Huiyuan to camp with Sheng at East Wei Bridge, claiming Sheng's force was too small to hold the rebels alone, to form pincers.

sentences.zh: 懷光雖不欲遣，且辭窮，無以沮解。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang, though unwilling to send them, was at the end of his arguments and could not obstruct and dissolve it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang, though unwilling, had no argument left to refuse.

sentences.zh: 帝猶豫曰：「晟移屯，懷光固怏怏，若又遣建徽等俱東，彼且為辭。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated: "If Sheng moves camp, Huaiguang will surely be displeased; if Jianhui and the others are also sent east, he will have his excuse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated: "If Sheng moves, Huaiguang will be displeased; if Jianhui and the others go east too, he will have his excuse.

sentences.zh: 少須之。」

translations.literal: Wait a little.
translations.idiomatic: Wait a little.

sentences.zh: 晟已徙營，不閱旬，懷光果奪兩節度兵。

translations.literal: Sheng had already moved camp; within less than ten days Huaiguang indeed seized the troops of the two commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had already moved; within ten days Huaiguang seized the troops of both commissioners.

sentences.zh: 建徽挺身免，惠元死之。

translations.literal: Jianhui escaped by throwing himself forward; Huiyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Jianhui escaped; Huiyuan was killed.

sentences.zh: 行在震驚，遂徙幸梁。

translations.literal: The temporary court was shaken and therefore moved the seat of rule to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The court was shaken and moved to Liang.

sentences.zh: 道有獻瓜果者，帝嘉其意，欲授以試官。

translations.literal: On the road someone presented melons and fruit; the emperor praised his intent and wished to grant a probationary office.
translations.idiomatic: On the road someone presented melons and fruit; the emperor was pleased and wished to grant a probationary office.

sentences.zh: 贄曰：「爵位，天下公器，不可輕也。」

translations.literal: Zai said: "Rank and office are the public vessels of all under Heaven and cannot be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zai said, "Rank is the public vessel of the realm and cannot be lightly given.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「試官虛名，且已與宰相議矣，卿其無嫌。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A probationary office is an empty name, and I have already discussed it with the chancellor—do not begrudge it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A probationary office is an empty title, and I have already discussed it with the chancellor—do not object."

sentences.zh: 贄奏：「信賞必罰，霸王之資也；

translations.literal: Zai submitted: "Trustworthy reward and certain punishment are the capital of hegemony and kingship;
translations.idiomatic: Zai submitted: "Trustworthy reward and certain punishment are the foundation of kingship;

sentences.zh: 輕爵褻刑，衰亂之漸也。

translations.literal: light rank and profane punishment are the beginning of decline and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: light rank and careless punishment are the beginning of decline.

sentences.zh: 非功而獲爵則輕，非罪而肆刑則褻。

translations.literal: To obtain rank without merit is to make rank light; to extend punishment without crime is to make punishment profane.
translations.idiomatic: Rank without merit makes rank cheap; punishment without crime makes punishment contemptible.

sentences.zh: 天寶之季，嬖幸傾國，爵以情授，賞以寵加，綱紀始壞矣。

translations.literal: In the late Tianbao era favorites overturned the state; rank was granted by affection, reward by favor—and regulation began to break.
translations.idiomatic: In late Tianbao, favorites overturned the state; rank came by affection, reward by favor—and order began to break.

sentences.zh: 羯胡乘之，遂亂中夏。

translations.literal: The Jiehu took advantage and thus threw the central plains into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took advantage and threw the central plains into chaos.

sentences.zh: 財賦不足以供賜，而職官之賞興焉；

translations.literal: When wealth and levies were insufficient to supply gifts, the reward of office titles arose;
translations.idiomatic: When funds could not supply gifts, offices were sold for reward;

sentences.zh: 職員不足以容功，而散、試之號行焉。

translations.literal: when office posts were insufficient to contain merit, the designations of probationary and irregular appointment arose.
translations.idiomatic: when posts could not contain merit, probationary titles arose.

sentences.zh: 今所病者爵輕也，設法貴之，猶恐不重，若又自棄，將何勸焉？

translations.literal: What is now afflicted is that rank is light; if you set laws to make it precious, one still fears it is not heavy enough—if you again abandon it yourself, how will you encourage men?
translations.idiomatic: The disease is that rank is too cheap; laws make it precious, yet you still fear it is not weighty enough—if you abandon it yourself, how will you encourage men?

sentences.zh: 陛下謂試官為虛名，豈思之未熟邪？

translations.literal: Your Majesty says probationary office is an empty name—have you not thought deeply enough?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty calls probationary office an empty name—have you not thought deeply enough?

sentences.zh: 夫立國惟義與權，誘人惟名與利。

translations.literal: To establish a state relies only on righteousness and expedient power; to entice men relies only on name and profit.
translations.idiomatic: To establish a state relies on righteousness and expedient power; to move men relies on name and profit.

sentences.zh: 名近虛，於教為重；

translations.literal: Name is near the empty—in teaching it is heavy;
translations.idiomatic: Name is near the empty—in moral teaching it weighs heavily;

sentences.zh: 利近實，於德為輕。

translations.literal: profit is near the real—in virtue it is light.
translations.idiomatic: profit is near the real—in virtue it weighs lightly.

sentences.zh: 凡所以裁是非，立法制，則存乎其義；

translations.literal: Whatever cuts right and wrong and establishes law and regulation rests in righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever judges right and wrong and establishes law rests in righteousness;

sentences.zh: 參虛實，揣輕重，則存乎其權。

translations.literal: whatever joins empty and real and weighs light and heavy rests in expedient power.
translations.idiomatic: whatever weighs empty against real rests in expedient power.

sentences.zh: 專實利而不濟之以虛，則物有匱耗而不給矣；

translations.literal: Devote only to real profit without assisting it with the empty, then things will be depleted and insufficient;
translations.idiomatic: Devote only to real profit without the empty, and resources will be exhausted;

sentences.zh: 專虛名而不副之以實，則情有誕謾而不趨矣。

translations.literal: devote only to empty name without matching it with the real, then feeling will be extravagant and false and men will not hasten to it.
translations.idiomatic: devote only to empty name without the real, and men will not strive for it.

sentences.zh: 故錫貨財，列稟秩，以彰實也；

translations.literal: Therefore bestowing goods and wealth and arraying salaries is to display the real;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore bestowing wealth and salary displays the real;

sentences.zh: 差品列，異服章，以飾虛也。

translations.literal: distinguishing ranks and varying dress and insignia is to adorn the empty.
translations.idiomatic: distinguishing ranks and dress adorns the empty.

sentences.zh: 居上者達其變，相須以為表裏，則為國之權得矣。

translations.literal: For one above to penetrate these changes and rely on one another as outer and inner—that is to obtain the power of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler who grasps these changes and uses them as outer and inner obtains the power of the state.

sentences.zh: 案甲令，有職事官、有散官、有勛官、有爵號。

translations.literal: According to the statutes, there are regular offices, irregular offices, merit offices, and noble titles.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes provide regular offices, irregular offices, merit offices, and noble titles.

sentences.zh: 其賦事受奉者，惟職事一官，以敘才能，以位勛德，所謂施實利而寓虛名也；

translations.literal: Those who perform duties and receive salaries have only the one regular office, to order talent and position merit and virtue—this is called applying real profit while lodging empty name;
translations.idiomatic: Those who perform duties receive only the regular office, ordering talent and merit—applying real profit while lodging empty name;

sentences.zh: 勛、散、爵號，止於服色、資蔭，以馭崇貴，以甄功勞，所謂假虛名佐實利者也。

translations.literal: merit, irregular, and noble titles extend only to dress and inheritance to control honor and assess achievement—this is called borrowing empty name to assist real profit.
translations.idiomatic: merit, irregular, and noble titles govern dress and inheritance—borrowing empty name to assist real profit.

sentences.zh: 今員外、試官與勛、散、爵號同，然而突铦鋒、排禍難者以是酬之可謂重矣。

translations.literal: Now probationary and irregular offices are the same as merit, irregular, and noble titles—yet to reward those who break sharp points and repel calamity with these may be called heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Probationary offices now equal merit titles—yet to reward those who risk their lives with these might seem generous.

sentences.zh: 今獻瓜一器、果一盛則受之，彼忘軀命者有以相謂矣，曰：『吾之軀命乃同瓜果。』

translations.literal: Now for presenting one vessel of melons or one basket of fruit one receives it—those who forget body and life will say to one another: 'My body and life are the same as melons and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Now one vessel of melons or one basket of fruit wins reward—those who risk their lives will say, 'Our lives are worth no more than melons and fruit.

sentences.zh: 瓜果，草木也。

translations.literal: Melons and fruit are grasses and trees.
translations.idiomatic: Melons and fruit are mere plants.

sentences.zh: 若草木然，人何勸哉？

translations.literal: If treated like grasses and trees, how will men be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: If lives are treated like plants, how will men be encouraged?

sentences.zh: 夫田父野人必欲得其歡心，厚賜之可也。」

translations.literal: A farmer in the fields who wishes to win their hearts may be richly gifted—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: A farmer who wishes to win hearts may be richly rewarded—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 俄以勞遷諫議大夫，仍為學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred for merit to remonstrating censor, still serving as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to remonstrating censor while remaining an academician.

sentences.zh: 時鳳翔節度使李楚琳殺張鎰得位，雖數貢奉，議者頗言其挾兩端，有所狙伺然。

translations.literal: At that time Li Chulin, military commissioner of Fengxiang, killed Zhang Yin and seized his post. Though he repeatedly sent tribute, discussants said he held two ends and was watching for an opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chulin of Fengxiang had killed Zhang Yin and seized his post. Though he sent tribute, many said he wavered between two sides and watched for opportunity.

sentences.zh: 帝亦不能容，其使至，皆不得召，欲以渾瑊代之。

translations.literal: The emperor also could not tolerate him; when his envoys arrived they were all not summoned. He wished to replace him with Hun Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not tolerate him; his envoys were not received. He wished to replace him with Hun Jian.

sentences.zh: 贄諫曰：「楚琳之罪舊矣，今議者乃始紛紜，不亦晚哉？

translations.literal: Zai remonstrated: "Chulin's crime is old; for discussants now only to grow clamorous—is it not late?
translations.idiomatic: Zai remonstrated: "Chulin's crime is long known; for counselors to grow clamorous only now—is it not late?

sentences.zh: 且勤王之師在畿內者，急宣亟告，景刻不可差。

translations.literal: Moreover the armies loyal to the throne within the capital region—urgent proclamations must be dispatched without delay of a single moment.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal armies near the capital need urgent orders without a moment's delay.

sentences.zh: 商嶺既回遠，而駱谷又為賊所扼，通王命者唯褒斜爾。

translations.literal: Shang Pass is already remote, and Luo Valley is again blocked by rebels; the only route for imperial commands is Baoxie.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Pass is remote and Luo Valley is blocked by rebels; imperial commands can pass only through Baoxie.

sentences.zh: 若復阻，則諸鎮之向背者，我勝則來，賊勝遂往，此焉幾會，不容差跌。

translations.literal: If it is again blocked, then the inclinations of the various commands—when we win they come, when the rebels win they go—this is a critical juncture that cannot be mishandled.
translations.idiomatic: If that route is blocked, the commands will follow victory—when we win they come, when rebels win they go—a critical juncture that cannot be mishandled.

sentences.zh: 使楚琳逞憾，敢為猖狂，南塞要沖，東與賊合，則我咽喉梗而心膂分矣，豈不病哉！

translations.literal: If Chulin vents his resentment and dares to act wildly, blocking the southern passes and joining the rebels in the east, then our throat is choked and heart and backbone divided—how is this not grave!
translations.idiomatic: If Chulin vents resentment and blocks the southern passes while joining rebels in the east, our throat is choked and our strength divided—how grave that would be!

sentences.zh: 今顧望兩端，是乃天誘其衷，通歸塗，濟大業也。」

translations.literal: Now to look about with two ends is Heaven tempting his inmost heart, opening the road of return to complete the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: His wavering is Heaven opening his heart to return and complete the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 帝釋然，盡召見其使，優詔勞安之。

translations.literal: The emperor was relieved and summoned all their envoys, bestowing gracious edicts to comfort and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was reassured, summoned all their envoys, and sent gracious edicts of comfort.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以內外從官普號「定難元從功臣」。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to give all inner and outer attendants the title collectively of 'Meritorious Followers Who Settled the Difficulty.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to give all inner and outer attendants the collective title 'Meritorious Followers Who Quelled the Crisis.'

sentences.zh: 贄曰：「宮官具寮，恪居奔走，勞則有之，何功之雲？

translations.literal: Zai said: 'Palace officials and full staff, respectful in attendance and running about—there is toil, but what merit is there?
translations.idiomatic: Zai said, 'Palace attendants serve faithfully—there is labor, but what merit is there?

sentences.zh: 難則嘗之，何定之雲？

translations.literal: They tasted hardship, but what settling is there?
translations.idiomatic: They shared hardship, but what quelling is there?

sentences.zh: 今與奮命者齒，恐沮戰士之心，結勛臣之憤。」

translations.literal: Now to rank them with those who strove with their lives fears discouraging warriors' hearts and arousing meritorious ministers' anger.
translations.idiomatic: To rank them with men who risked their lives will discourage warriors and anger meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 京師已平，帝欲召渾瑊訪奔亡內人，給裝使赴行在。

translations.literal: The capital had been pacified. The emperor wished to summon Hun Jian to inquire after palace women who had fled, provide funds and send them to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was pacified. The emperor wished to summon Hun Jian to find palace women who had fled and send them to the court.

sentences.zh: 贄諫曰：「大難始平，而百役疲瘵之氓、重傷殘廢之卒，皆忍死扶疾，想聞德音。

translations.literal: Zai remonstrated: 'Great hardship has just been pacified, while the people of the hundred services, worn and afflicted, and soldiers heavily wounded and disabled, all endure death and support illness, longing to hear virtuous sound.
translations.idiomatic: Zai remonstrated: 'The great crisis has just ended. Wounded soldiers and exhausted people long to hear the emperor's voice.

sentences.zh: 蓋事有先後，義有輕重，重者宜先，輕者宜後。

translations.literal: Affairs have precedence and afterward; righteousness has weight and lightness—the weighty should come first, the light afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs have order of priority; the weighty should come first, the light afterward.

sentences.zh: 昔武王克殷，有未下車而為之者，有下車而為之者。

translations.literal: Of old, when King Wu overcame Yin, there were things done before descending from the chariot and things done after descending.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu overcame Yin, some acts came before he left his chariot, some after.

sentences.zh: 當今所務，謂宜以大臣馳傳，迎復神主，脩飭郊丘，展禋享之禮，申告謝之意；

translations.literal: What should be attended to now, I say, is that great ministers should post relays to welcome and restore the imperial ancestral tablets, repair suburban altars, extend sacrificial rites, and declare thanksgiving;
translations.idiomatic: The urgent tasks are to send great ministers to recover the ancestral tablets, repair the suburban altars, perform sacrifices, and give thanks;

sentences.zh: 恤死義，犒有功，崇進忠直，優問耆耄；

translations.literal: comfort the dead in righteousness, reward the meritorious, promote the loyal and upright, and kindly inquire after the aged;
translations.idiomatic: comfort the righteous dead, reward merit, promote the loyal, and honor the aged;

sentences.zh: 定反側，寬脅從，官失職，復廢業，是皆宜先不可後也。

translations.literal: settle the turning and the two-faced, widen those coerced to follow, restore offices lost and revive abandoned enterprises—these all should come first and cannot come after.
translations.idiomatic: settle waverers, pardon the coerced, restore offices and revive livelihoods—all these must come first.

sentences.zh: 葺宮室，治服玩，耳目之娛，巾櫛之侍，是皆宜後不可先也。

translations.literal: Repair palace halls, manage dress and playthings, pleasures for eyes and ears, attendants for comb and towel—these all should come after and cannot come first.
translations.idiomatic: Repair palaces, manage dress and ornaments, pleasures and personal attendants—all these must come after.

sentences.zh: 且內人當離潰之後，或為將士所私。

translations.literal: Moreover, after the scattering of flight, palace women may have been taken privately by officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: After the flight, palace women may have been taken by soldiers.

sentences.zh: 昔人掩絕纓、飲盜馬者，豈忘其愛邪？

translations.literal: Men of old who covered the dangling tassel and drank the stolen horse—did they forget their affection?
translations.idiomatic: Men of old who forgave minor offenses—did they forget affection?

sentences.zh: 知為君之體然也。

translations.literal: They knew what it was to be a ruler's substance.
translations.idiomatic: They knew what it meant to be a ruler.

sentences.zh: 天下固多褻人，何必獨此？」

translations.literal: All under Heaven certainly has many base persons—why must it be only these?
translations.idiomatic: The realm has many base men—why fix on these alone?

sentences.zh: 帝不復下詔，猶遣使諭瑊資遣。

translations.literal: The emperor no longer issued the edict, yet still sent envoys to instruct Jian to provide funds and dispatch them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not issue the edict, but still sent envoys to Jian to provide funds.

sentences.zh: 初，劉從一、姜公輔等材下不逮贄遠甚，徒以單言暫謀偶有合，由下位建臺宰。

translations.literal: At first Liu Congyi, Jiang Gongfu, and others were far inferior in talent to Zai, yet because a single word or brief plan occasionally accorded, they rose from low position to chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congyi, Jiang Gongfu, and others were far less able than Zai, yet occasional agreement raised them from low posts to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 而贄孤立一意，為左右權幸沮短，又言事無所回諱，陰失帝意，久之不得宰相。

translations.literal: Zai stood alone in one intent; favored ones on left and right obstructed and belittled him. Moreover his words on affairs knew no evasion or taboo, secretly losing the emperor's favor—long he could not obtain the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Zai stood alone; favorites obstructed him. His frank counsel secretly lost the emperor's favor, and long he could not become chancellor.

sentences.zh: 還京，但為中書舍人。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he was only a drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he served only as secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 母韋猶在江東，帝遣中人迎還京師。

translations.literal: His mother Wei was still in Jiangdong; the emperor sent a palace envoy to welcome her back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Wei was still in the lower Yangzi; the emperor sent an envoy to bring her to the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄以喪解官，客東都。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he left office for mourning and lodged in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left office for mourning and stayed in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 諸方赗遺一不取，惟韋臯以布衣交，先以聞，故所致輒稱詔受之。

translations.literal: Gifts from the various regions he accepted none; only Wei Gao, who had known him as a commoner, sent first with notice, and therefore what he sent Zai could accept as by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted no gifts from the regions except from Wei Gao, an old friend who notified the court first so his gifts could be accepted as imperial bounty.

sentences.zh: 又詔中人護父柩至自吳會，葬洛陽。

translations.literal: Also an edict sent palace envoys to escort his father's coffin from Wu and Kuaiji to bury in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent envoys to escort his father's coffin from the southeast for burial in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 服除，以權知兵部侍郎復召為學士。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned again as academician with provisional authority as vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was recalled as academician and provisional vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 入謝，伏地鯁泣，帝為興，改容慰撫。

translations.literal: Entering to give thanks, he prostrated himself and choked with weeping; the emperor was moved, changed expression, and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Entering to give thanks, he wept prostrate; the emperor was moved and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 眷遇彌渥，天下屬以為相，而竇參素不平，忌之。

translations.literal: Favor grew ever deeper; all under Heaven looked to him as chancellor, while Dou Can had long been displeased and envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Favor deepened; the realm expected him as chancellor, while Dou Can envied him.

sentences.zh: 贄亦數言參罪失。

translations.literal: Zai also repeatedly spoke of Can's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Zai also repeatedly reported Can's faults.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年，罷學士，以兵部侍郎知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenyuan he was removed as academician and made vice minister of war in charge of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 7 he left the Hanlin post and became vice minister of war overseeing examinations.

sentences.zh: 明年，參黜，乃以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The next year Can was dismissed, and then he was made Secretariat vice director and Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Can was dismissed, and Zai became vice director and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 帝始任楊炎、盧杞，引樹私黨，排忠良，天下怨疾。

translations.literal: The emperor at first employed Yang Yan and Lu Qi, drawing private factions and excluding the loyal and worthy—all under Heaven resented it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had employed Yang Yan and Lu Qi, building factions and excluding the loyal—the realm resented it.

sentences.zh: 貞元後，懲艾其失，雖置宰相，至除用庶官，反覆參詰乃得下。

translations.literal: After Zhenyuan he corrected these errors; though he set chancellors, even appointing common officials required repeated examination and questioning before approval.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenyuan he corrected these errors; even minor appointments required repeated scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 及贄秉政，始請臺閣長官得自薦其屬，有不職，坐舉者。

translations.literal: When Zai held power he first asked that Secretariat and Censorate chiefs might recommend their own subordinates, and if they were unfit, the recommender would be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zai asked that department chiefs recommend their own subordinates, with punishment for bad recommendations.

sentences.zh: 帝初許之，或言諸司所引皆親黨，招賂遺，無實才，帝復詔宰相自擇。

translations.literal: The emperor at first permitted it, but some said those recommended by the offices were all kin and clique, accepting bribes without real talent. The emperor again ordered chancellors to choose themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, but others said offices recommended only kin and bribe-takers. He ordered chancellors to choose instead.

sentences.zh: 贄奏言：「齊桓公問管仲害霸，對曰：『得賢不能任，害霸也；

translations.literal: Zai submitted: 'Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong what harms hegemony. He answered: To obtain the worthy yet not employ them harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: Zai cited Guan Zhong: to obtain the worthy but not employ them harms hegemony;

sentences.zh: 任賢不能固，害霸也；

translations.literal: to employ the worthy yet not secure them harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: to employ them but not secure them harms hegemony;

sentences.zh: 固始而不終，害霸也；

translations.literal: to secure them at the start yet not continue to the end harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: to secure them at first but not to the end harms hegemony;

sentences.zh: 與賢人謀事，而小人議之，害霸也。』

translations.literal: to plan affairs with worthy men yet have petty men discuss them harms hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: to plan with worthy men while petty men discuss it harms hegemony.

sentences.zh: 所謂小人者，非悉懷險诐以覆邦家也，蓋趨向狹促，以沮議為出眾，自異為不群，趣小利，昧遠圖，效小信，傷大道爾。

translations.literal: What are called petty men are not all who harbor danger and deceit to overturn state and family; mostly they are narrow in orientation, take obstructing counsel as standing out, take being different as not joining the crowd, run after small profit, are blind to far designs, effect small trust, and injure the great Way.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men are not all traitors; many are narrow, take obstruction for distinction, chase small profit, and injure the great Way.

sentences.zh: 所謂臺省長官，仆射、尚書、丞、郎、御史大夫、中丞是也。

translations.literal: What are called Secretariat and Censorate chiefs—vice directors, ministers, assistants, directors, censor-in-chief, and vice censor-in-chief—are they.
translations.idiomatic: These are the Secretariat and Censorate chiefs.

sentences.zh: 陛下擇輔相多出其中，行實不能頓殊也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty chooses chief ministers mostly from among them; conduct cannot suddenly differ.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty chooses chancellors from among them; conduct cannot suddenly differ.

sentences.zh: 今乃謂不能進一二屬吏，豈後位宰相則可擇天下材乎？

translations.literal: Now to say they cannot advance one or two subordinate officials—can later-position chancellors then choose talent from all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: If they cannot recommend one or two subordinates, can chancellors alone choose talent from the realm?

sentences.zh: 夫求才者貴廣，考課者貴精。

translations.literal: In seeking talent what is prized is breadth; in examination what is prized is precision.
translations.idiomatic: In seeking talent breadth matters; in examination precision matters.

sentences.zh: 往武後收人心，務拔擢，非徒人得薦士，亦許自舉其才，豈不易哉？

translations.literal: Of old Empress Wu won hearts and strove for promotion—not only might men recommend scholars, they might also recommend their own talent. Was that not easy?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu won hearts by broad promotion—men could recommend others or themselves. Was that not easy?

sentences.zh: 然而課責嚴，進退速，故當世稱知人之明，累朝賴多士之用。

translations.literal: Yet examination and responsibility were strict, advancement and dismissal swift—therefore the age praised discernment of men, and successive courts relied on many scholars' use.
translations.idiomatic: Yet examination was strict and turnover swift—the age praised her discernment and later courts relied on her scholars.

sentences.zh: 陛下賞鑒獨任，難於公舉，有登延之路，無練核之方。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's judgment relies solely on personal appointment; it is hard to obtain by public recommendation. There is a road of advancement but no method of training and verification.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty relies on personal judgment, hard to obtain by public recommendation; there is advancement but no verification.

sentences.zh: 武後以易得人，陛下以精失士。

translations.literal: Empress Wu lost men by ease; Your Majesty loses men by excessive refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu lost men through ease; Your Majesty loses men through excessive refinement.

sentences.zh: 今擇宰相以重於庶品，選長官以愈於下流。

translations.literal: Now to choose chancellors is heavier than common ranks, to choose chiefs heavier than lower streams.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors are chosen more carefully than common ranks, chiefs more carefully than subordinates.

sentences.zh: 及宰相獻言，長吏薦士，則又納橫議，廢始謀，是任以重者輕其言，待以輕者重其事也。」

translations.literal: Yet when chancellors offer words and chiefs recommend scholars, then horizontal criticism is accepted and initial plans abandoned—this is to treat the weighty lightly in their words and treat the light heavily in their affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when chancellors speak and chiefs recommend, criticism overturns the plan—treating the weighty lightly and the light heavily.

sentences.zh: 帝雖嘉之，然卒停薦士詔。

translations.literal: The emperor though he praised this yet in the end stopped the edict recommending scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this but ended the recommendation edict.

sentences.zh: 舊制，吏部選以歲集。

translations.literal: By old regulation the Board of Civil Office selected annually in assembly.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation the Board of Civil Office selected annually.

sentences.zh: 乾元後，天下兵興，率三年一調，吏員稽壅，則案牒叢淆，偽冒蒙真，吏緣以為奸，廢置無綱，至十年不被調者，缺員或累歲不補。

translations.literal: After Qianyuan, with warfare throughout the realm, generally selection came once in three years. Official posts piled up, then dossiers were confused in heaps; falsehood and impersonation covered truth, and clerks used this for corruption. Appointment lacked regulation, and some went ten years without selection while vacancies sometimes accumulated years without filling.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianyuan selection came every three years; dossiers piled up, fraud flourished, and some waited ten years without appointment.

sentences.zh: 贄乃請以內外員三分之，每歲計闕集人，檢柅吏奸，天下便之。

translations.literal: Zai then asked that inner and outer posts be divided in thirds, each year calculating vacancies to assemble candidates, inspecting and restraining clerkly corruption—all under Heaven found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zai divided posts into thirds, counted vacancies yearly, and restrained clerkly fraud—the realm approved.

sentences.zh: 當是時，賈耽、盧邁、趙憬同輔政，凡有司關白，三人者更相顧不肯判。

translations.literal: At this time Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Zhao Jing jointly assisted in government. Whenever a bureau submitted for approval, the three looked at one another and would not sign.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Zhao Jing shared power; when bureaus submitted matters, the three refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 贄又請如故事，旬一人秉筆，所咨輒判。

translations.literal: Zai again asked that by old story one man each ten days hold the brush; whatever was consulted he would decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zai asked that by old custom one man hold the brush each ten days and decide all submissions.

sentences.zh: 又以西北邊歲調河南、江淮兵，謂之「防秋」，士不素練，戰數敗，將統制不一，亡以應敵。

translations.literal: Also on the northwest frontier troops were levied yearly from Henan and the Huai and Yangzi regions, called 'autumn defense.' Soldiers were not trained by habit; battles were repeatedly lost. Command was not unified and there was no means to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest troops were levied yearly from the east, called 'autumn defense.' Untrained troops repeatedly lost; command was divided.

sentences.zh: 乃上陳其弊曰：

translations.literal: He therefore submitted listing the defects, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted listing the defects:

sentences.zh: 自祿山構亂，肅宗始撤邊備，以靖中邦，借外威，寧內難，於是吐蕃乘釁，回紇矜功，中國不振，四十餘年。

translations.literal: From the time Lushan raised rebellion, Suzong first withdrew frontier defenses to pacify the central states, borrowing outer might to quiet inner difficulty—thereupon Tibet seized the opening, Huihe boasted of merit, and China did not recover for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Since An Lushan's rebellion, frontier defenses were withdrawn to pacify the center; Tibet and the Uyghurs seized advantage, and China did not recover for forty years.

sentences.zh: 率傷耗之民，竭力以事，西輸賄繒，北償馬資，尚不足滿其意。

translations.literal: Leading injured and depleted people, they exhausted strength in service; west they transported silks and brocades, north they repaid horse payments—still insufficient to fill their desire.
translations.idiomatic: Exhausted people paid tribute west and north—still insufficient.

sentences.zh: 於是調斂四方，以屯疆陲，又不能遏其侵。

translations.literal: Then levies were gathered from the four quarters to garrison the frontier, yet still could not check their raids.
translations.idiomatic: Levies from the four quarters garrisoned the frontier yet could not stop raids.

sentences.zh: 故小入則驅略，深入則戒嚴。

translations.literal: Therefore small entries meant plunder and drive; deep entries meant alarm and strict defense.
translations.idiomatic: Small raids plundered; deep raids brought alarm.

sentences.zh: 於時議安邊者，皆務所難，忽所易，勉所短，略所長，行之而要不精，圖之而功靡就。

translations.literal: At that time those who discussed securing the frontier all strove for what was difficult, neglected what was easy, urged what was short, overlooked what was long—practiced and essentials were not refined; planned and achievement did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier planners strove for the difficult, neglected the easy, and achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 夫勢有難易，事有先後。

translations.literal: Situation has difficulty and ease; affairs have precedence and afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Situation has difficulty and ease; affairs have order.

sentences.zh: 力大而敵脆，則先所難，是謂奪人之心也；

translations.literal: Strength great and foe fragile—then first the difficult; this is called seizing men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When strength is great and the foe fragile, take the difficult first—seize their hearts.

sentences.zh: 力寡而敵堅，則先所易，是謂觀釁而動也。

translations.literal: Strength few and foe firm—then first the easy; this is called observing openings and moving.
translations.idiomatic: When strength is few and the foe firm, take the easy first—watch for openings.

sentences.zh: 今財匱於中，人勞未瘳，而欲發師徒以犯獵寇境，復其侵疆，攻其堅城，前有勝負未必之虞，後有饋運不繼之患。

translations.literal: Now wealth is depleted in the center, men's toil not yet healed, yet you wish to send armies to invade nomad territory, recover invaded borders, attack their firm cities—before there is the uncertainty of victory or defeat, behind there is the worry that supply will not continue.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth is depleted and the people unhealed, yet armies are sent to invade nomad lands, recover borders, and attack strong cities—with uncertain victory and broken supply lines.

sentences.zh: 萬一橈敗，適所以啟戎心，挫國威也。

translations.literal: If by any chance there is defeat, it will precisely open nomad hearts and bruise national prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat would embolden the nomads and bruise national prestige.

sentences.zh: 以此安邊，可謂不量勢而務所難矣。

translations.literal: To secure the frontier thus may be called not measuring strength and striving for what is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: To secure the frontier this way is to ignore strength and strive for the difficult.

sentences.zh: 天之授有分，地之產有宜，是以五方之俗，長短各殊。

translations.literal: Heaven's grant has division; earth's production has fitness—therefore the customs of the five regions, long and short, each differ.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's grant and earth's fitness differ—the five regions' customs differ.

sentences.zh: 勉所短而敵長者殆，用所長而乘短者強。

translations.literal: To urge what is short and match the enemy's long is perilous; to use what is long and ride over what is short is strong.
translations.idiomatic: To use weakness against the enemy's strength is perilous; to use strength against weakness prevails.

sentences.zh: 且以水草為居，討獵為生，便於馳突，不恥敗亡，此戎狄所長，中國之短也。

translations.literal: Moreover to take water and grass as dwelling and hunting as livelihood suits sudden charge and does not shame defeat—this is what the Rong and Di excel in and China falls short.
translations.idiomatic: Nomads live on pasture and hunting, excel at sudden charge and do not fear defeat—China's weakness.

sentences.zh: 而欲益兵搜乘，爭驅角力，交鋒原野之上，決命尋常之間，以此禦寇，可謂勉所短而校其長矣。

translations.literal: Yet you wish to increase troops and search out chariots, compete in driving and measuring strength, cross blades on the open plain and decide life in ordinary encounter—to defend against invaders thus may be called urging what is short and matching their long.
translations.idiomatic: Yet China increases troops and fights on open ground—urging weakness against their strength.

sentences.zh: 務所難，勉所短，勞費百倍，終無成功，雖果成之，不挫則廢。

translations.literal: Striving for the difficult, urging the short—expense a hundredfold greater, in the end no success; even if it succeeds, without setback it is abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Striving for the difficult costs a hundredfold and fails; even success cannot be sustained.

sentences.zh: 誠以越天授，違地產，虧時勢，以反物宜者也。

translations.literal: Truly this is to cross Heaven's grant, violate earth's production, lose the season's advantage, and go against things' fitness.
translations.idiomatic: This crosses Heaven's grant, violates earth's fitness, and goes against nature.

sentences.zh: 胡不守所易，用所長乎？

translations.literal: Why not keep to what is easy and use what is long?
translations.idiomatic: Why not keep to the easy and use what is long?

sentences.zh: 若乃擇將吏，脩紀律，訓齊師徒；

translations.literal: If one chooses generals and officials, repairs discipline, and trains and aligns armies;
translations.idiomatic: Choose good generals, repair discipline, train armies;

sentences.zh: 耀德以佐威，能邇以示遐；

translations.literal: display virtue to assist awe, show ability near to indicate distance;
translations.idiomatic: display virtue to support awe, show near strength to warn the far;

sentences.zh: 禁侵暴以彰吾信，抑攻取以昭吾仁；

translations.literal: forbid aggression and violence to manifest our trust, restrain attack and seizure to manifest our benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: forbid aggression to show trust, restrain seizure to show benevolence;

sentences.zh: 彼求和則善之而勿與盟，彼為寇則備之而不報復。

translations.literal: if they seek peace then treat them well and do not make alliance with them; if they act as invaders then prepare against them and do not retaliate.
translations.idiomatic: if they seek peace, receive them without alliance; if they raid, prepare without revenge.

sentences.zh: 此當今所易也。

translations.literal: These are what is easy at present.
translations.idiomatic: These are the easy measures of the present.

sentences.zh: 賤力貴智，好生惡殺；

translations.literal: Value wisdom and despise force; love life and hate killing;
translations.idiomatic: Value wisdom over force; love life and hate killing;

sentences.zh: 輕利重人，忍小全大；

translations.literal: treat light profit heavily and men lightly; endure the small to preserve the great;
translations.idiomatic: value men over profit; endure the small to preserve the great;

sentences.zh: 安其居而動，俟其時後行。

translations.literal: settle their dwelling before moving; wait for the time before acting.
translations.idiomatic: settle the people before moving; wait for the right time.

sentences.zh: 脩封疆，守要害，蹊塹隧，列屯營，謹禁防，明斥候，務農足食，非萬全不謀，非百克不鬥；

translations.literal: Repair borders, guard strategic points, trench roads and tunnels, array camps and garrisons, strict prohibition and defense, clear scouts and watches, devote to farming for full food, plan only when wholly safe, fight only when a hundred victories are certain;
translations.idiomatic: Repair borders, guard passes, trench roads, array camps, farm for food, plan only when safe, fight only when certain;

sentences.zh: 寇小至則遏其入，寇大至則邀其歸，據險以乘之，多方以誤之，使其勇無所加，眾無所用，掠則靡獲，攻則不能，進有腹背支敵之虞，退有首尾不相救之患。

translations.literal: if invaders come small then check their entry; if invaders come large then intercept their return, take advantage of terrain to ride over them, use many stratagems to mislead them, so that their courage has nowhere to apply and their masses nowhere to be used—plunder then nothing gained, attack then cannot succeed; advancing they have worry of front and rear and supporting enemies, retreating they have the trouble of head and tail not rescuing one another.
translations.idiomatic: if raiders come small, block them; if large, cut off their return, use terrain and stratagem so they gain nothing and cannot advance or retreat safely.

sentences.zh: 是謂乘其弊，不戰而屈人兵。

translations.literal: This is called riding their weakness and subduing men's armies without battle.
translations.idiomatic: This is to exploit their weakness and subdue them without battle.

sentences.zh: 此中國之長也。

translations.literal: This is China's strength.
translations.idiomatic: This is China's strength.

sentences.zh: 我之所長，戎狄之短也；

translations.literal: What we excel in is the Rong and Di's shortcoming;
translations.idiomatic: What we excel in is the nomads' weakness;

sentences.zh: 我之所易，戎狄之難也。

translations.literal: what is easy for us is difficult for the Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: what is easy for us is difficult for them.

sentences.zh: 以長制短，則用力寡而見功多；

translations.literal: To use the long to control the short—then little force and much achievement seen;
translations.idiomatic: Use strength against weakness—little force, great effect;

sentences.zh: 以易敵難，則財不匱而事速成。

translations.literal: to use the easy to meet the difficult—then wealth not depleted and affairs quickly completed.
translations.idiomatic: use the easy against the difficult—wealth spared, success swift.

sentences.zh: 舍此不務而反為所乘，斯謂倒持戈矛，以鐏授寇者也。

translations.literal: Abandon this and not attend to it yet turn to be ridden by them—this is called holding the spear reversed and giving the butt to the invader.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon this and instead be ridden by them is to hold the spear by the blade and hand it to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今皆務之矣，尚且守封未固，寇戎未懲者何邪？

translations.literal: Now all attend to this, yet still borders are not secure and nomad invaders are not chastised—why?
translations.idiomatic: All this is now urged, yet borders are not secure—why?

sentences.zh: 病在謀無定用，眾無適從；

translations.literal: The disease lies in plans without fixed use, masses without suitable following;
translations.idiomatic: The disease is plans without fixed use and the masses without direction;

sentences.zh: 任者不必才，才者不必任；

translations.literal: those employed are not necessarily talented, the talented not necessarily employed;
translations.idiomatic: the employed are not necessarily able, the able not necessarily employed;

sentences.zh: 聞不必實，實不必聞；

translations.literal: what is heard is not necessarily real, what is real is not necessarily heard;
translations.idiomatic: what is heard is not necessarily true, what is true is not necessarily heard;

sentences.zh: 所信不必誠，所誠不必信；

translations.literal: those trusted are not necessarily sincere, those sincere are not necessarily trusted;
translations.idiomatic: those trusted are not necessarily sincere, the sincere not necessarily trusted;

sentences.zh: 行不必當，當不必行。

translations.literal: action is not necessarily fitting, what is fitting is not necessarily acted on.
translations.idiomatic: action is not necessarily right, what is right is not necessarily done.

sentences.zh: 又有六失焉。

translations.literal: There are also six losses.
translations.idiomatic: There are also six failures.

sentences.zh: 夫兵有攻討，有鎮守。

translations.literal: Armies have attack and chastisement, and garrison and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Armies may attack or garrison.

sentences.zh: 權以紓難，暫以應機，事有便宜，謀有奇詭，不恤常制，不徇眾情，死生進退，唯將所命，攻討之兵也。

translations.literal: Authority to ease difficulty, temporary response to opportunity—affairs have what is expedient, plans have what is strange; not caring for regular regulation, not following popular feeling; life and death, advance and retreat, only as the general commands—this is the army of attack and chastisement.
translations.idiomatic: Expedient authority, temporary response, strange plans, life and death at the general's command—this is the attack army.

sentences.zh: 人情者，利焉則勸，習焉則安，保親戚而後樂生，顧家業而後忘死，可以治術馭，不可以法制驅，鎮守之兵也。

translations.literal: Human feeling: where there is profit men are encouraged; where there is habit men are at ease; they secure kin before enjoying life, look to family enterprise before forgetting death—can be governed by art, cannot be driven by law and regulation—this is the garrison army.
translations.idiomatic: Men fight for profit, settle by habit, protect kin before risking life—governed by art, not driven by law—this is the garrison army.

sentences.zh: 王者欲備封疆，禦戎狄，則選鎮守之兵以置之。

translations.literal: A king who wishes to prepare borders and defend against Rong and Di should select garrison armies and place them.
translations.idiomatic: A king securing borders should place garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 古之善選置者，必辨其土宜，察其技能，知其好惡。

translations.literal: Those skilled in selection and placement of old necessarily distinguished their soil's fitness, inspected their skills, and knew their likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled placement distinguished local conditions, skills, and preferences.

sentences.zh: 用其力，不違其性；

translations.literal: Used their strength without violating their nature;
translations.idiomatic: Used their strength without violating nature;

sentences.zh: 齊其俗，不易其宜；

translations.literal: aligned their customs without changing what was fitting;
translations.idiomatic: aligned customs without changing fitness;

sentences.zh: 引其善，不責其所不能；

translations.literal: led their goodness without demanding what they could not do;
translations.idiomatic: encouraged their strengths without demanding the impossible;

sentences.zh: 禁其非，不處其所不欲。

translations.literal: forbade their wrongs without placing them in what they did not wish.
translations.idiomatic: forbade wrongs without forcing what they rejected.

sentences.zh: 類其部伍，安其家室，然後能使之樂其居，定其誌。

translations.literal: Classed their companies, settled their households—then could make them enjoy their dwelling and fix their will.
translations.idiomatic: Grouped them properly, settled their families—then they would serve willingly.

sentences.zh: 以惠則感而不驕，以威則肅而不死。

translations.literal: With kindness they were moved and not arrogant; with awe they were respectful and did not flee.
translations.idiomatic: Kindness moved them without pride; awe kept them without flight.

sentences.zh: 靡督課而自用，馳禁防而不攜。

translations.literal: Without supervision and examination they acted on their own; released prohibitions and defenses without disaffection.
translations.idiomatic: Without constant inspection they served willingly; without harsh restrictions they stayed loyal.

sentences.zh: 故守則固，戰則強。

translations.literal: Therefore in defense they were firm, in battle strong.
translations.idiomatic: In defense they were firm; in battle, strong.

sentences.zh: 其術無它，便於人而已。

translations.literal: The method has nothing else—convenience for men alone.
translations.idiomatic: The method is simply convenience for men.

sentences.zh: 今遠調屯士，以戍邊陲，邀所不能，強所不欲，廣其數不考於用，責其力不察其情，斯可為羽衛之儀，而無益備禦之實也。

translations.literal: Now distant troops are transferred to garrison the frontier, inviting what they cannot, forcing what they do not wish; broadening their numbers without examining use, demanding their strength without inspecting feeling—this may serve as guard ceremony but brings no real benefit to defense.
translations.idiomatic: Sending distant troops to garrison the frontier forces the unwilling and untrained—ceremony without real defense.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 窮邊之地，千里蕭條，寒風裂膚，豺狼為鄰，晝則荷戈以耕，夜則倚烽以覘，有剽害之慮，無休暇之娛，非生其域、習其風，幼而視焉，長而安焉，則不能寧居而狎其敵也。

translations.literal: In exhausted border lands, a thousand li are desolate; cold wind splits the skin, wolves and jackals are neighbors; by day they carry spears to plow, by night lean on beacon fires to watch; there is worry of sudden harm, no leisure for rest—not born in that region, accustomed to that wind, viewing it from childhood and at ease from youth—then they cannot dwell in peace and be familiar with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Border lands are desolate and harsh; men not born there cannot dwell in peace or know the enemy.

sentences.zh: 關東百物阜殷，士忲溫飽，比諸邊隅，不翅天地。

translations.literal: East of the Pass the hundred things are rich and abundant; scholars are warm and fed. Compared with border corners, it is not merely heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Pass life is rich and easy—compared with the frontier, another world.

sentences.zh: 聞絕塞荒陬，則辛酸動容；

translations.literal: Hearing of remote passes and wild regions, they are moved to bitterness on their faces;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of remote wastes, they wince;

sentences.zh: 聆強蕃勁虜，則懾駭褫情。

translations.literal: hearing of strong fan states and fierce foes, they are startled and their courage is stripped.
translations.idiomatic: hearing of fierce enemies, their courage fails.

sentences.zh: 又使去親族，舍園廬，甘所辛酸，抗所懾駭，將冀為用，不亦疏乎？

translations.literal: Moreover they are made to leave kin and clan, abandon gardens and huts, willingly taste bitterness and resist what startles them—yet you expect them to be useful: is it not far-fetched?
translations.idiomatic: Made to leave home for hardship and terror—yet expected to serve well: is that not absurd?

sentences.zh: 又有休代之期，無統制之善，資奉姑息，譬如驕子，進不邀以成功，退不處以嚴憲，屈指計歸，張頤待飼，師一挫傷，則乘其危橈，布路東潰。

translations.literal: Also there are periods of rest and rotation without good unified command; support and provision are indulgent, like a spoiled child—on advance they are not invited to merit by success, on retreat they are not placed under strict discipline. Counting fingers they calculate return, opening mouths they await feeding; once the army suffers a setback, they seize the crisis and scatter east along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Rotation without unified command, indulgent supply like spoiling children—after one defeat they scatter east.

sentences.zh: 平居殫資儲以奉浮冗，臨難棄城鎮以搖疆場。

translations.literal: In peace they exhaust stores to support floating excess; in crisis they abandon cities and garrisons to shake the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In peace they consume stores for useless men; in crisis they abandon posts.

sentences.zh: 其弊豈特無益哉？

translations.literal: Is the harm only that there is no benefit?
translations.idiomatic: The harm is worse than mere uselessness.

sentences.zh: 謫徙之人，本以增戶實邊，立功自贖。

translations.literal: Exiled and transferred men were originally to increase households and fill the border, establishing merit to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles were meant to fill the border and redeem themselves by merit.

sentences.zh: 既無良之人，而思亂幸災又甚於戍卒，適有防衛之煩，而無立功之益。

translations.literal: Since there are no good men, those who think of disorder and hope for calamity are worse than garrison soldiers—they have the trouble of defense without the benefit of establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles are worse than garrison troops—burden without benefit.

sentences.zh: 雖前代行之，固非可遵者也。

translations.literal: Though former ages practiced this, it is certainly not to be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Former ages did this, but it should not be followed.

sentences.zh: 帥臣身不臨邊，而以偏師戍守。

translations.literal: Commanders personally do not arrive at the border yet garrison with partial armies.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders do not go to the border themselves but send partial forces.

sentences.zh: 大抵士之犀銳，悉選以自奉，委疲羸者以守要沖，寇至而不支，則劫執芟蹂，恣所欲得，比都府聞之，虜已旋返。

translations.literal: Mostly the sharp and keen among soldiers are all selected for their own service; tired and weak are entrusted with guarding strategic points. When invaders arrive they cannot support, then they are seized, slaughtered, and ravaged at will; when the metropolitan office hears, the raiders have already turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders keep the best troops and leave the weak at key points—when raiders come, posts fall before help arrives.

sentences.zh: 治兵若此，斯可謂措置乖方。

translations.literal: To manage troops thus may be called placement contrary to method.
translations.idiomatic: Such troop management is misplaced.

sentences.zh: 一失也。

translations.literal: The first loss.
translations.idiomatic: The first failure.

sentences.zh: 賞以存勸，罰以示懲，以懋有庸，以威不恪。

translations.literal: Reward is to preserve encouragement; punishment is to show chastisement—to urge those with merit, to awe those not respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Reward encourages; punishment awes—the meritorious and the disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 故賞罰之於馭眾，譬輗軏所以行車，銜勒所以服馬也。

translations.literal: Therefore reward and punishment in controlling the masses are like crossbar and linchpin for moving a cart, bit and bridle for subduing a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Reward and punishment are like linchpin and bridle for controlling troops.

sentences.zh: 今將之號令不能行之軍，國之典刑不能施之將，上下遵養，以茍歲時。

translations.literal: Now generals' orders cannot be carried out in the army; the state's penal code cannot be applied to generals—above and below mutually indulge to get through the year.
translations.idiomatic: Generals' orders fail in the army; penal law fails on generals—all indulge to pass the year.

sentences.zh: 欲褒一有功，慮無功者怨，嫌疑而不賞；

translations.literal: Wishing to praise one who has merit, one fears those without merit will resent—suspicion and no reward;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing resentment, the meritorious go unrewarded;

sentences.zh: 欲責一有罪，畏同惡者竦，隱忍而不誅。

translations.literal: wishing to punish one who has crime, one fears those of the same evil will be startled—concealment and no execution.
translations.idiomatic: fearing alarm, the guilty go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 故忘身效節者抵噪於眾，僨軍緩救者畜奸不畏，褒貶稱毀，紛然相亂。

translations.literal: Therefore those who forget body and show loyalty are met with clamor from the masses; those who ruin armies and slow rescue harbor treachery without fear. Praise, blame, reputation, and slander swirl in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal are mocked; the treacherous go unpunished—praise and blame are confused.

sentences.zh: 公者直己不求諸人，則罹困厄；

translations.literal: The upright straighten themselves and do not seek from others—then they meet hardship;
translations.idiomatic: The upright suffer hardship;

sentences.zh: 奸者行私茍媚於眾，則取優崇。

translations.literal: the crafty act privately and fawn on the masses—then they obtain preferment and honor.
translations.idiomatic: the crafty fawn on others and win favor.

sentences.zh: 此義士勇夫所以痛心解體也。

translations.literal: This is why men of righteousness and brave husbands are heartbroken and dismembered in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: This breaks the hearts of loyal warriors.

sentences.zh: 又如遇敵而守不固，陳謀而功不成。

translations.literal: Again, when meeting the enemy defense is not firm, when laying plans achievement is not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Defense fails; plans fail.

sentences.zh: 責將帥，將帥曰資糧不足；

translations.literal: Blame the generals—the generals say funds and grain are insufficient;
translations.idiomatic: Blame generals—they say supplies are short;

sentences.zh: 責有司，有司曰須給無乏；

translations.literal: blame the offices—the offices say requisitions and provision are not lacking;
translations.idiomatic: blame offices—they say supplies are ample;

sentences.zh: 更相為解，而朝廷含糊，未嘗究詰。

translations.literal: each explains for the other while the court is vague and never investigates.
translations.idiomatic: each excuses the other while the court never investigates.

sentences.zh: 故抱直者吞聲，罔上者不慚。

translations.literal: Therefore the upright swallow their voices and those who deceive the throne are not ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The upright are silenced; deceivers feel no shame.

sentences.zh: 馭眾若此，可謂課責虧度。

translations.literal: To control the masses thus may be called examination and responsibility deficient in measure.
translations.idiomatic: Such control means failed accountability.

sentences.zh: 二失也。

translations.literal: The second loss.
translations.idiomatic: The second failure.

sentences.zh: 以課責之虧，措置之乖，將不得竭其才，卒不得盡其力，屯集雖眾，無施戰陣，虜常橫行，以謂境無人焉。

translations.literal: From deficient examination and misplaced arrangement, generals cannot exhaust their talent and soldiers cannot exhaust their strength—though masses gather, none can be deployed in battle array. Invaders constantly range freely, saying the border has no men.
translations.idiomatic: Failed accountability and bad placement leave talent unused—masses gather yet the frontier seems empty.

sentences.zh: 吏習其常，惟曰兵少不敵，朝廷莫之省，則又調發益師，無裨於備禦，而有弊於供億。

translations.literal: Officials are accustomed to the usual and only say troops are few and cannot match the enemy; the court does not examine it, then again transfers and increases armies—no help to defense, yet harm to supply.
translations.idiomatic: Officials say troops are too few; the court sends more—no help to defense, more burden on supply.

sentences.zh: 閭井日耗，斂求日繁，傾家析產，榷鹽稅酒，無慮所入半以事邊。

translations.literal: Hamlets and wells daily decline, levies daily multiply; families are broken and estates divided—salt monopoly and wine tax, reckoning that half of revenue goes to the border.
translations.idiomatic: Villages decline and levies multiply—half of revenue goes to the border.

sentences.zh: 制用若此，可謂財匱於兵眾矣。

translations.literal: To manage expenditure thus may be called wealth depleted on armies and masses.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditure thus depletes the realm on armies.

sentences.zh: 三失也。

translations.literal: The third loss.
translations.idiomatic: The third failure.

sentences.zh: 今四夷最強盛者，莫如吐蕃。

translations.literal: Of the four barbarians now, the strongest is none other than Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Of the four barbarians, Tibet is strongest.

sentences.zh: 舉吐蕃眾，未當中國十數大郡，而內虞外備與中國不殊，所以能寇邊者無幾。

translations.literal: Take Tibet's masses—they do not equal a dozen great commanderies of China—yet inner alarm and outer defense are not different from China. Those able to raid the border are few.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet's population is smaller than a dozen Chinese commanderies, yet raids continue.

sentences.zh: 又器不犀利，甲不精完，材不趨敏。

translations.literal: Moreover weapons are not sharp, armor not refined and complete, material not quick and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Their weapons are not sharp, armor not strong, men not agile.

sentences.zh: 動則中國慹其眾不敢抗，靜則憚其強不敢侵，何哉？

translations.literal: When they move, China fears their masses and dares not resist; when they are still, China dreads their strength and dares not invade—why?
translations.idiomatic: China fears them in motion and dreads them at rest—why?

sentences.zh: 良以我之節制多，而彼之統帥一也。

translations.literal: Truly because our regulation is many and their command unified.
translations.idiomatic: Because our command is divided and theirs unified.

sentences.zh: 且節制多，則人心不一；

translations.literal: When regulation is many, hearts are not one;
translations.idiomatic: Many regulators mean divided hearts;

sentences.zh: 人心不一，則號令不行；

translations.literal: when hearts are not one, orders are not carried out;
translations.idiomatic: divided hearts mean orders fail;

sentences.zh: 號令不行，則進退難必；

translations.literal: when orders are not carried out, advance and retreat are hard to be certain;
translations.idiomatic: failed orders make advance and retreat uncertain;

sentences.zh: 進退難必，則疾徐失宜；

translations.literal: when advance and retreat are hard to be certain, speed and slowness miss their fit;
translations.idiomatic: uncertainty makes timing fail;

sentences.zh: 疾徐失宜，則機會不及；

translations.literal: when speed and slowness miss their fit, opportunity is not reached;
translations.idiomatic: missed timing loses opportunity;

sentences.zh: 機會不及，則氣勢自衰。

translations.literal: when opportunity is not reached, momentum naturally declines.
translations.idiomatic: lost opportunity drains momentum.

sentences.zh: 斯乃勇廢為尫，眾失為弱。

translations.literal: Then courage is abandoned for weakness and masses lose strength.
translations.idiomatic: Courage fades and strength is lost.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶時，制西北二蕃，則朔方、河西、隴右三節度而已，尚慮權分，或詔兼領之。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao era, to regulate the two fan of the northwest there were only the three commands of Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou—and still they feared divided authority, sometimes ordering concurrent command.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan and Tianbao, only three northwest commands regulated the frontier—yet authority was still divided.

sentences.zh: 中興未遑外討，則僑四鎮隸安定，以隴右附扶風，所當二蕃，則朔方、涇原、隴右、河東四節度而已，以關東戍卒屬之。

translations.literal: In restoration there was no leisure for outer campaigns, so four commands were placed under Anding, Longyou attached to Fufeng—against the two fan, only Shuofang, Jingyuan, Longyou, and Hedong four commands, with eastern garrison soldiers subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: In restoration, four commands with eastern garrison troops faced the frontier.

sentences.zh: 雖任未得人，而措置之法存焉。

translations.literal: Though appointments were not always the right men, the method of arrangement remained.
translations.idiomatic: Though men were not always right, the method remained.

sentences.zh: 自賊泚亂以誘涇原，懷光反以汙朔方，則分朔方為三節度，其鎮軍且四十，皆特詔任之，各有中人監軍，鹹得相抗。

translations.literal: From Ze Chao's rebellion tempting Jingyuan and Huaiguang's revolt defiling Shuofang, Shuofang was divided into three commands, garrison armies nearly forty—all specially appointed by edict, each with a palace eunuch supervising the army, all able to resist one another.
translations.idiomatic: After rebellions, Shuofang was split into three commands and nearly forty garrisons, each with eunuch supervisors resisting one another.

sentences.zh: 既無軍法臨下，莫能稟屬，邊書告急，方使關白用兵，是謂從容拯溺，揖讓救焚矣。

translations.literal: Since there was no military law governing those below, none could receive subordination. When frontier letters reported urgency, then they were told to report for permission to use troops—this is called leisurely saving the drowning and bowing in salute to rescue the burning.
translations.idiomatic: Without military law, none obeyed; urgent reports waited on court approval—leisurely rescue of drowning men.

sentences.zh: 兵以氣若勢為用者也，氣聚則盛，散則消；

translations.literal: Armies use spirit like momentum; when spirit gathers it flourishes, when scattered it vanishes;
translations.idiomatic: Armies live on spirit; gathered it flourishes, scattered it fades;

sentences.zh: 勢合則威，析則弱。

translations.literal: when momentum combines it is awesome, when divided weak.
translations.idiomatic: combined momentum is strong, divided weak.

sentences.zh: 今之邊戍，勢弱氣消。

translations.literal: Now frontier garrisons have weak momentum and vanished spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrisons are weak in momentum and spirit.

sentences.zh: 建軍若此，可謂力分於將多矣。

translations.literal: To establish armies thus may be called strength divided among many generals.
translations.idiomatic: Such armies divide strength among too many generals.

sentences.zh: 四失也。

translations.literal: The fourth loss.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth failure.

sentences.zh: 治戎之要，在均齊而已。

translations.literal: The essential of governing the Rong is in equalizing and balancing alone.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the frontier requires balance.

sentences.zh: 故軍法無貴賤之差、多少之異，所以同其誌、盡其力也。

translations.literal: Therefore military law has no difference of noble and base, much and little—thus to make their wills one and exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Military law knows no rank or number—all must serve alike.

sentences.zh: 被邊長鎮之兵，皆百戰傷夷，角所能則習，度所處則危，考服役則勞，察臨敵則勇，然衣稟止於當身，又為家室所分，居常凍餒。

translations.literal: Soldiers of long frontier commands are all hundred-battle wounded; comparing ability they are practiced, estimating position they are in peril, examining service they are toiled, observing facing the enemy they are brave—yet clothing and grain suffice only for the body and are again divided for household; in ordinary times they freeze and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier veterans are skilled and brave yet freeze and hunger, their rations divided for family.

sentences.zh: 而關東戍士，歲月更代，怯於應敵，懈於服勞，然衣稟優厚，繼以茶藥，資以蔬醬。

translations.literal: Yet eastern garrison soldiers, replaced yearly, are timid facing the enemy and slack in service—yet clothing and grain are generously thick, continued with tea and medicine, supplied with vegetables and sauce.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern garrison troops, rotated yearly, are timid yet richly supplied with food, tea, and medicine.

sentences.zh: 豐寡相縣，勢則遠甚。

translations.literal: Abundance and scarcity are suspended; the disparity in situation is very far.
translations.idiomatic: The disparity is extreme.

sentences.zh: 又有以邊軍詭為奏請遙隸神策者，稟賜之饒，有三倍之益。

translations.literal: Also some falsely petition that frontier armies be remotely attached to the Shence, with generous rations and benefits threefold.
translations.idiomatic: Some frontier troops falsely attach to the Shence and receive triple rations.

sentences.zh: 此士類所以忿恨，經費所以褊匱。

translations.literal: This is why soldiers resent and expenditures are narrow.
translations.idiomatic: This breeds resentment and strains funds.

sentences.zh: 夫事業未異，給養頓殊，人情所不甘也。

translations.literal: Affairs are not different yet provision suddenly differs—what human feeling will not resent?
translations.idiomatic: Same service, different pay—who would not resent?

sentences.zh: 不為戎首，已可嘉者，況使協力同心，以攘寇難，臣知有所不能焉。

translations.literal: Not to be leaders of the Rong is already praiseworthy; how much more to make them cooperate in one heart to repel invader difficulty—I know it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: That they do not rebel is already praise; expecting united effort against invaders is impossible.

sentences.zh: 養士若此，可謂怨生於不均矣。

translations.literal: To nourish soldiers thus may be called resentment born from inequality.
translations.idiomatic: Such treatment breeds resentment from inequality.

sentences.zh: 五失也。

translations.literal: The fifth loss.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth failure.

sentences.zh: 凡任將帥，必先考察行能，然後指所授之方、所委之要，令自揣可否，以見要領。

translations.literal: Whenever appointing generals, one must first examine conduct and ability, then point to the quarter entrusted and the key entrusted, and have them measure whether they can or cannot, to see the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint generals only after examining conduct and ability, then define their mission clearly.

sentences.zh: 須某甲兵，藉某參屬，用若干步騎，計若干資糧，何所列屯，何時成功，觀其言，校其實。

translations.literal: Need certain armor and troops, borrow certain staff, use so many foot and horse, reckon so much funds and grain, what posts to array, what time to succeed—observe their words, verify the fact.
translations.idiomatic: Specify troops, staff, supplies, posts, and deadlines—then verify performance.

sentences.zh: 若曰不足取，當艱之於初，不宜詒悔於後也；

translations.literal: If they say not sufficient to take, press the difficulty at the start—do not deceive with regret afterward;
translations.idiomatic: If unfit, reject at the start—do not regret later;

sentences.zh: 若曰可任，則當要之於終，不宜掣肘於內也。

translations.literal: if they say can be entrusted, then hold them to the end—do not restrain from within.
translations.idiomatic: if fit, trust to the end—do not interfere from within.

sentences.zh: 故疑者不使，使者不疑。

translations.literal: Therefore the doubtful are not employed; the employed are not doubted.
translations.idiomatic: Do not employ the doubtful; do not doubt the employed.

sentences.zh: 勞神於拔選，端拱於委任，然後核否臧，信賞罰，受賞者不為濫，當罰者不敢辭，付授專則茍且之心息矣。

translations.literal: Exhaust spirit on selection, sit upright in delegation—then examine good and bad, trust reward and punishment. Those rewarded are not excessive; those punished dare not excuse. Delegation specialized and the heart of expediency rests.
translations.idiomatic: Select carefully, delegate fully, then reward and punish fairly—expediency ceases.

sentences.zh: 是以古之遣將者，君推轂而命之，又賜鈇鉞，故軍容不入國，國容不入軍，機宜不以遠決，號令不以兩從。

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity when sending generals, the ruler pushed the chariot wheel and commanded them, also bestowing axe and yue—thus military bearing did not enter the state and state bearing did not enter the army; expedient measures were not decided from afar, orders were not twofold.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers entrusted generals fully—military and civil spheres separate, orders not divided.

sentences.zh: 今陛下命帥，先求易制者，多其部使力分，輕其任使心弱。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty orders commanders, first seeking those easy to control, multiplying their departments to divide strength, lightening their commission to weaken heart.
translations.idiomatic: Now the throne seeks easily controlled commanders, multiplies deputies, and weakens authority.

sentences.zh: 由是分閫責成之義廢，死綏任咎之誌衰。

translations.literal: From this the meaning of entrusting frontier responsibility is abandoned and the will to die in harness and bear blame declines.
translations.idiomatic: Thus responsibility is abandoned and the will to die for duty fades.

sentences.zh: 一則聽命，二則聽命，止取承順可矣，若有意乎靖難則不可。

translations.literal: First obey orders, second obey orders—only take compliance and that is enough; if there is intent to pacify difficulty, it cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: Obey orders, obey orders—compliance suffices; real pacification cannot.

sentences.zh: 兩強相接，兩軍相持，事機所急，罅不留息，況千里之遠，九重之深，陳述之難明，聽覽之不專，欲事無遺策，雖聖亦有所不能焉。

translations.literal: When two strengths meet and two armies stand opposed, the urgency of opportunity leaves no gap for breath—how much more when a thousand li distant and nine layers deep, statement hard to clarify and listening not concentrated—wishing affairs without omitted strategy, even a sage cannot.
translations.idiomatic: In battle, moments count—how can distant court deliberation decide?

sentences.zh: 守戍者以寡不敢抗，分鎮者以無詔不敢救，逗留之頃，寇已奔逼。

translations.literal: Garrison defenders with few dare not resist; divided commanders without edict dare not rescue—in the delay of lingering, invaders have already pressed close.
translations.idiomatic: Few defenders dare not fight; divided commanders dare not rescue—delay lets raiders escape.

sentences.zh: 牧馬屯牛，鞠椎剽矣；

translations.literal: Herding horses and penning cattle, they beat clubs and plundered;
translations.idiomatic: They drove off horses and cattle and plundered;

sentences.zh: 嗇夫樵婦，罄俘囚矣。

translations.literal: frugal husbands and firewood-gathering wives were exhausted as captives.
translations.idiomatic: even common folk were taken captive.

sentences.zh: 假令詔至發兵，更相顧望，莫敢遮礙，敗者減百為一，獲者衍百為千。

translations.literal: Suppose an edict arrives to dispatch troops—they look at one another and dare not obstruct; the defeated are reduced from a hundred to one, the captors multiplied from a hundred to a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When troops are dispatched, they hesitate; defeat shrinks armies while plunder swells raiders.

sentences.zh: 帥守以總制在朝，不恤於罪；

translations.literal: Commanders and defenders, because overall control is at court, do not care about guilt;
translations.idiomatic: Commanders, knowing control rests at court, fear no blame;

sentences.zh: 陛下以權出己，不究厥情。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because authority issues from yourself, does not investigate the facts.
translations.idiomatic: the throne, holding authority, does not investigate.

sentences.zh: 用帥若此，可謂機失於遙制矣。

translations.literal: To use commanders thus may be called opportunity lost through distant control.
translations.idiomatic: Using commanders thus loses opportunity through distant control.

sentences.zh: 六失也。

translations.literal: The sixth loss.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth failure.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂宜罷四方之防秋者，以其數析而三之：其一，責本道節度，募壯士願屯邊者徙焉；

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly holds that the autumn defense troops of the four quarters should be abolished, their numbers divided in three: one part, charge the original circuit commissioner to recruit stalwart men willing to garrison the border and transfer them there;
translations.idiomatic: I propose abolishing autumn defense levies and dividing forces three ways: local commissioners recruit willing border settlers;

sentences.zh: 其一，則第以本道衣稟，責關內、河東募用蕃、夏子弟願傅軍者給焉；

translations.literal: one part, then simply use the original circuit's clothing and grain, charge Guannei and Hedong to recruit and employ sons of fan and Xia willing to attach to the army and supply them;
translations.idiomatic: Guannai and Hedong recruit frontier peoples with local rations;

sentences.zh: 其一，以所輸資糧給應募者，以安其業。

translations.literal: one part, use the submitted funds and grain to pay those who respond to recruitment, to settle their enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: submitted grain pays recruits to settle them.

sentences.zh: 詔度支市牛，召工就諸屯繕完器具。

translations.literal: Order the Department of Public Works to buy cattle and summon craftsmen to the various garrisons to repair and complete tools.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury should buy cattle and send craftsmen to garrisons.

sentences.zh: 至者家給牛一，耕耨水火之器畢具，一歲給二口糧，賜種子，勸之播蒔。

translations.literal: On arrival each household is given one ox; plow, hoe, fire, and water tools are all provided. Each year two persons' grain is given, seed bestowed, and planting urged.
translations.idiomatic: Each family receives an ox, tools, grain for two persons yearly, and seed for planting.

sentences.zh: 須一年，則使自給，有餘粟者，縣官倍價以售。

translations.literal: After one year they support themselves; if there is surplus grain, the county office buys at double price.
translations.idiomatic: After one year they feed themselves; surplus grain is bought at double price.

sentences.zh: 既息調發之煩，又無幸免之弊，出則人自為戰，處則家自為耕。

translations.literal: Both the trouble of transfer levies ceases and the defect of exemption ends; abroad men fight on their own, at home families farm on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Levy troubles cease; men fight abroad and farm at home.

sentences.zh: 與夫暫屯遽罷，豈同日論哉！

translations.literal: Compared with sudden garrison and hasty withdrawal—is it the same day of discussion!
translations.idiomatic: This is nothing like sudden garrison and hasty withdrawal!

sentences.zh: 然後建文武大臣一人為隴右元帥，自涇、隴、鳳翔薄長武城，盡山南西道，凡節度府之兵皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Then establish one civil and military great minister as Longyou supreme commander, from Jing, Long, and Fengxiang pressing to Changwu city, through all of Shannan West Circuit—all military commissioners' troops subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Then appoint one Longyou supreme commander over western frontier armies;

sentences.zh: 又詔一人為朔方元帥，由鄜坊、邠寧揵靈夏，凡節度府之兵屬焉。

translations.literal: Also order one man as Shuofang supreme commander, from Bin and Ning pressing Ling and Xia—all military commissioners' troops subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: one Shuofang commander over the north;

sentences.zh: 又詔一人為河東元帥，舉河東，極振武，節度府之兵屬焉。

translations.literal: Also order one man as Hedong supreme commander, raising Hedong to the limit of Zhenwu—all military commissioners' troops subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: one Hedong commander over the east.

sentences.zh: 各以臨邊要州為治所，所部州若府，遴柬良吏為刺史，外奉軍興，內課農桑，慎守中國所長，謹行當今所易，則八利可致，六失可去矣。

translations.literal: Each takes a border strategic prefecture as seat of government; of subordinate prefectures and offices, select good officials as prefects—outwardly serving military exigency, inwardly enforcing farming and sericulture, carefully keeping what China excels in and prudently practicing what is easy today—then the eight benefits can be attained and the six losses removed.
translations.idiomatic: Each should govern border prefectures with good officials, promote farming, use China's strengths and easy measures—then eight benefits come and six losses depart.

sentences.zh: 帝愛重其言，不從也。

translations.literal: The emperor cherished and valued his words but did not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his words but did not follow them.

sentences.zh: 班宏判度支，卒官，贄薦李巽，帝漫許之，而自用裴延齡。

translations.literal: Ban Hong judged the Department of Public Works and died in office. Zai recommended Li Xun; the emperor casually agreed yet personally used Pei Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong died in office; Zai recommended Li Xun, but the emperor chose Pei Yanling.

sentences.zh: 贄言：「延齡僻戾躁妄，不可用。」

translations.literal: Zai said: 'Yanling is perverse, violent, and reckless—he cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: Zai said Yanling was perverse and reckless and could not be used.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 俄而延齡奸佞得君，天下仇惡，無敢言。

translations.literal: Shortly Yanling, treacherous and fawning, won the ruler; all under Heaven hated him and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yanling won favor; the realm hated him and none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 贄上書苦諫，帝不懌，竟以太子賓客罷。

translations.literal: Zai submitted memorials bitterly remonstrating; the emperor was displeased and in the end dismissed him as guest of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zai remonstrated bitterly; the emperor was displeased and dismissed him as guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 贄本畏慎，未嘗通賓客。

translations.literal: Zai was by nature fearful and cautious and never received guests.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was cautious and never received guests.

sentences.zh: 延齡揣帝意薄，讒短百緒，帝遂發怒，欲誅贄，賴陽城等交章論辨，乃貶忠州別駕。

translations.literal: Yanling guessed the emperor's favor was thin and slandered him in a hundred threads; the emperor then grew angry and wished to execute Zai. Thanks to Yang Cheng and others submitting memorials in debate, he was demoted to vice prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling slandered him; the emperor wished to execute him until Yang Cheng and others saved him by demotion to Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 後稍思之，會薛延為刺史，諭旨慰勞。

translations.literal: Later the emperor gradually reflected. When Xue Yan became prefect, he conveyed imperial intent to comfort and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor relented; Xue Yan as prefect was sent to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 韋臯數上表請贄代領劍南，帝猶銜之，不肯與。

translations.literal: Wei Gao repeatedly submitted tables asking Zai to lead Jiannan in his place; the emperor still harbored resentment and would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao repeatedly asked that Zai lead Jiannan; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，召還。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong succeeded, Zai was recalled.

sentences.zh: 詔未至，卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: The edict had not arrived when he died, age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, he died at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded minister of war and given the posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of war with the title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 始，贄入翰林，年尚少，以材幸，天子常以輩行呼而不名。

translations.literal: At first, when Zai entered the Hanlin, he was still young; because of talent he was favored—the Son of Heaven often called him by generation rank without name.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai entered the Hanlin he was young and favored; the emperor called him by generation rank without using his name.
