sentences.zh: 在奉天，朝夕進見，然小心精潔，未嘗有過，由是帝親倚，至解衣衣之，同類莫敢望。

translations.literal: At Fengtian he was received morning and evening, yet careful and refined, never having fault—therefore the emperor relied on him personally, even removing his own garment to clothe him; none of his kind dared hope for it.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengtian he served morning and evening without fault; the emperor even gave him his own garment—none dared hope for such favor.

sentences.zh: 雖外有宰相主大議，而贄常居中參裁可否，時號「內相」。

translations.literal: Though outwardly there were chancellors presiding over great deliberation, Zai often stood in the center judging yes and no; at the time he was called 'inner chancellor.'
translations.idiomatic: Though chancellors presided outwardly, Zai judged affairs at center and was called the inner chancellor.

sentences.zh: 嘗為帝言：「今盜遍天下，宜痛自咎悔，以感人心。

translations.literal: He once said to the emperor: 'Now bandits fill all under Heaven; you should sternly blame yourself and repent to move men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor: 'Bandits fill the realm; you must repent deeply to move hearts.

sentences.zh: 昔成湯罪己以興，楚昭王出奔，以一言善復國。

translations.literal: Of old Cheng Tang blamed himself and flourished; King Zhao of Chu went into exile, and with one good word restored the state.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tang blamed himself and rose; King Zhao of Chu restored his state with one good word.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠不吝改過，以言謝天下，使臣持筆亡所忌，庶叛者革心。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly does not begrudge reforming faults and with words apologizes to all under Heaven, so that your servant holding the brush has nothing to fear, perhaps rebels will change heart.
translations.idiomatic: If you reform and apologize to the realm, rebels may change heart.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 故奉天所下制書，雖武人悍卒無不感動流涕。

translations.literal: Therefore the proclamations issued at Fengtian—even fierce soldiers and hardy troops were all moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Proclamations at Fengtian moved even fierce soldiers to tears.

sentences.zh: 後李抱真入朝，為帝言：「陛下在奉天、山南時，赦令至山東，士卒聞者皆感泣思奮。

translations.literal: Later Li Baozhen entered court and said to the emperor: 'When Your Majesty was at Fengtian and Shannan, amnesty edicts reached Shandong—soldiers who heard them all wept and longed to strive.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen later said soldiers in Shandong wept and longed to fight when they heard the Fengtian edicts.

sentences.zh: 臣是時知賊不足平。」

translations.literal: Your servant at that time knew the bandits could not be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: I knew then the rebels could not stand.

sentences.zh: 議者謂興元戡難功，雖爪牙宣力，蓋贄有助焉。

translations.literal: Discussants held that the achievement of Xingyuan in quelling difficulty, though claws and teeth exerted force, was largely aided by Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Discussants held that the Xingyuan restoration owed much to Zai.

sentences.zh: 狩山南也，道險澀，與從官相失，夜召贄不得，帝驚且泣，詔軍中得贄者賞千金。

translations.literal: On the hunt in Shannan the road was dangerous and narrow; he lost his attendants. At night he summoned Zai and could not obtain him—the emperor was alarmed and wept, ordering that whoever in the army found Zai would be rewarded a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: In Shannan he lost Zai at night, wept, and offered a thousand gold for finding him.

sentences.zh: 久之，上謁，帝喜見顏間，自太子以下皆賀。

translations.literal: After long time he presented himself; the emperor's pleased expression showed on his face—from the heir apparent down all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai appeared, the emperor rejoiced and all congratulated.

sentences.zh: 及輔政，不敢自顧重，事有可否必言之，所言皆剴拂帝短，懇到深切。

translations.literal: When he assisted in government he did not dare consider his own weight; if affairs had yes or no he necessarily spoke—what he spoke all cut against the emperor's faults, earnest and to the depth.
translations.idiomatic: In office he spoke frankly against the emperor's faults with earnest depth.

sentences.zh: 或規其太過者，對曰：「吾上不負天子，下不負所學，皇它恤乎？」

translations.literal: Some advised him he was too excessive; he answered: 'Above I do not fail the Son of Heaven, below I do not fail what I studied—what else is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: When told he was too harsh, he said he owed duty to heaven and to learning.

sentences.zh: 既放荒遠，常闔戶，人不識其面。

translations.literal: Once banished to the remote, he often closed his doors; men did not know his face.
translations.idiomatic: Banished, he closed his doors and was seldom seen.

sentences.zh: 又避謗不著書，地苦瘴癘，只為《今古集驗方》五十篇示鄉人雲。

translations.literal: Also avoiding slander he did not compose books. The land was bitter with miasma; he only made fifty chapters of Prescriptions Tested Ancient and Modern to show the villagers.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote no books in exile, only fifty chapters of tested medical prescriptions for his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：德宗之不亡，顧不幸哉！

translations.literal: The commentator says: That Dezong did not perish was yet unfortunate!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: That Dezong did not perish was itself a misfortune!

sentences.zh: 在危難時聽贄謀，及已平，追仇盡言，怫然以讒幸逐，猶棄梗。

translations.literal: In danger and hardship he listened to Zai's plans; once pacified he pursued grudges against all words, displeased and drove out the fawning favored by slander—still discarding the stem.
translations.idiomatic: In crisis he heard Zai; once safe he drove out loyal counsel and kept flatterers.

sentences.zh: 至延齡輩，則寵任磐桓，不移如山，昏佞之相濟也。

translations.literal: As for Yanling and his kind, then favor and employment lingered, immovable as a mountain—the benighted and fawning assisting one another.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yanling he favored immovably—the benighted and fawning together.

sentences.zh: 世言贄白罷翰林，以為與吳通玄兄弟爭寵，竇參之死，贄漏其言，非也。

translations.literal: The age says Zai himself left the Hanlin, thinking it was contention for favor with the brothers Wu Tongxuan; that in Dou Can's death Zai leaked his words—is not so.
translations.idiomatic: The claim that Zai left the Hanlin over rivalry with Wu Tongxuan, or leaked Dou Can's words, is false.

sentences.zh: 夫君子小人不兩進，邪諂得君則正士危，何可訾耶？

translations.literal: Gentleman and petty man cannot both advance; when the crooked and fawning win the ruler the upright are endangered—how can one blame?
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman and petty man cannot advance together; when flatterers win, the upright are endangered—why blame Zai?

sentences.zh: 觀贄論諫數十百篇，譏陳時病，皆本仁義，可為後世法，炳炳如丹，帝所用才十一。

translations.literal: View Zai's remonstrances in several tens and hundreds of chapters, satirizing and stating the ills of the time—all rooted in benevolence and righteousness, usable as law for later ages, bright as cinnabar—yet what the emperor used was only one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Zai's memorials, rooted in benevolence and righteousness, shine like cinnabar—yet the emperor used barely a tenth.

sentences.zh: 唐胙不競，惜哉！

translations.literal: Tang's sacrifice did not compete—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Tang's fortune failed to compete—alas!
